title: How Much Does an MTD Accountant Cost? What to Compare Before You Buy
excerpt: An MTD price only makes sense when you know which jobs it covers. A software subscription, quarterly filing service and accountant-managed package can involve very different responsibilities.
metaTitle: MTD Accountant Cost: Fees and What’s Included | TaxSimba
metaDescription: See dated MTD price examples and compare bookkeeping, quarterly updates, annual returns and catch-up charges before choosing accountant support.
featuredImageAlt: A client examines a price tag while an accountant explains the records and filing work included in a service.

sources.label: GOV.UK — choose the right software for making tax digital for income tax
GOV.UK — choose agents for making tax digital for income tax

content:
MTD fees vary with the work included. Published offers checked on 21 October 2026 included Taxfix plans at £4.99 a month for self-service software and £39.99 for full support, both including VAT. Those are one provider’s advertised offers, not a market average or a TaxSimba quote. Compare bookkeeping, quarterly updates, the annual return and any catch-up fees.

Start with the service, then compare the price

A £5 software subscription and a £40 managed service are not two prices for the same job. One may leave you to keep the books and file; the other may include that work. The useful question is: what will I still have to do after paying?

Published MTD price examples

These examples were checked on 21 October 2026. They are advertised offers from one provider, not a survey of UK fees. Taxfix listed self-service at £4.99 a month, assistance at £24.99 and full support at £39.99, including VAT. Its page distinguished client bookkeeping from accountant-managed work and advertised introductory free months. Read the current plans and conditions before using those figures to compare a quote.

Offers change. Check eligibility, the period covered, cancellation terms and what happens after an introductory offer. For a recurring quote, multiply the price by the number of payments, then add setup and agreed catch-up work. Do not compare one provider’s introductory period with another’s full-year total.

Five jobs your quote should name

  • Software and the income sources it supports.
  • Recording and reconciling transactions, including cash and platform fees.
  • Checking and sending each required quarterly update.
  • Preparing the annual return for the same tax year.
  • Dealing with earlier records, corrections and questions outside the package.

For example, a bookkeeper may maintain your records while an accountant files the return. That can work well, but confirm who joins up the information and whether both fees are in your budget.

What about TaxSimba’s price?

Use the current TaxSimba MTD packages for the actual offer. Describe each trade or property source and the updates already sent. Ask for any earlier-period work to be priced before it starts. This guide does not substitute a competitor’s price for a TaxSimba quote.

Your service fee is separate from your tax

Paying an accountant each month does not pay your Income Tax bill. Keep service invoices separate from payments to HMRC. If you are unsure whether MTD applies, check qualifying income first so you do not buy the wrong service.

Work out the cost over the same service period

Illustration, not provider quotes: offer A is £20 a month for 12 months, plus £120 setup and £180 catch-up work. Its total is £540. Offer B is £42 a month for 12 months with those jobs included: £504. These figures assume no further VAT is due. The lower monthly headline costs £36 more overall.

Use the quote comparison tool below with your own figures. Then mark each task as included, excluded or unclear. An unknown catch-up fee is not zero. Get it confirmed before using the total to choose.

Compare a monthly quote with an annual quote

Illustrative example.

Imagine two quotes covering the same twelve months, income sources and work. Quote A is £30 a month plus £180 for earlier-period work: £360 + £180 = £540. Quote B is £420 including that same earlier-period work. Assume both figures include any applicable VAT and no other charges. These are invented comparison figures, not TaxSimba prices.

The headline monthly price is not the total cost. Before choosing, ask whether earlier-period work is actually needed and whether each quote covers the same service period. A different scope makes the comparison invalid.

Actions to take
CheckPractical action
Monthly priceMultiply by the number of payments covering the agreed period.
Earlier-period workAsk which periods, records and corrections the extra fee covers.
Included filingsMatch each business, update and annual return on both quotes.

Is the lowest monthly fee the cheapest overall?

Only a comparison of the complete agreed work and charges can answer that. Record one-off fees and any applicable VAT alongside recurring payments.

What should a written quote identify?

The tax year, income sources, record-keeping responsibilities, included filings, payment schedule and triggers for extra work.

  • Monthly or annual total including applicable VAT
  • Earlier-period work and agreed charges
  • Who maintains records, checks figures and submits

title: How Much Does a Self Assessment Accountant Cost? Compare the Full Service
excerpt: The right Self Assessment fee depends on the work you need, not simply the number of pages in a return. Before choosing an accountant, ask what the price covers and what could be additional.
metaTitle: Self Assessment Accountant Cost and Fees | TaxSimba
metaDescription: Compare dated Self Assessment fee examples, VAT and the work included. Check income sources, specialist calculations and the complete quote.
featuredImageAlt: A business owner and accountant compare income records and the scope of a tax-return service.

sources.label: GOV.UK — check if you need tax return
GOV.UK — legal financial

content:
Published Self Assessment fees checked on 21 October 2026 included £179 plus VAT for RJ Accountancy’s basic return and £275 plus VAT at Sleek. These are examples, not an average or equivalent packages. Your quote depends on the income sources, records and extra calculations involved.

Two published fees—and why the scope matters

Checked on 21 October 2026, RJ Accountancy’s fee schedule listed a basic personal return at £179 plus VAT, with business accounts and rental calculations charged separately. Sleek’s guide advertised its Self Assessment service at £275 plus VAT. These are examples of actual advertised fees, not equivalent services or a UK average.

Confirm any VAT shown, eligibility and extra work with the provider. A quote for one straightforward income source should not be treated as a price for a property disposal, several years of missing returns or complex crypto calculations.

What should your own quote cover?

  • The tax year and each income source.
  • Preparation, questions, review and submission after your approval.
  • Whether business bookkeeping or rental calculations are included.
  • Any extra schedules, specialist calculations or earlier-year corrections.
  • The total payable, including applicable VAT, and when payment is due.

Keep the written quote. A larger headline discount is not useful if it leaves out the work you need. Company accounts are also separate from a director’s personal return.

Get a better quote by describing the job

For example: “I need my 2025/26 return, with PAYE income and one rental property. I have the P60 and agent statements. The property was not sold. Does the fee include the rental calculation and filing?” Add any overseas income, gains, missing records or HMRC notices before buying.

Can you deduct the accountant’s fee?

HMRC distinguishes business accountancy costs from preparing and submitting a personal Self Assessment return. Its guidance lists personal-return preparation and submission as non-allowable. If an invoice covers business accounts and personal-return work, ask for a clear description so any business element can be assessed; do not deduct the whole bill automatically.

Choosing TaxSimba

Check TaxSimba’s current SA packages for the actual price and included work. A fee pays for the agreed preparation and support. It cannot guarantee a refund: that depends on your income, reliefs and tax already paid.

Match the quote to your situation

Scope questions for different returns
Your situationWork to name in the quote
PAYE plus a small tradePersonal return, business profit calculation and any bookkeeping needed.
PAYE plus rental incomeRental calculation, ownership share and finance-cost treatment.
Property sold or investments disposed ofDisposal calculations and any separate property-reporting work.
Missing earlier yearsA price and filing plan for each year, rather than one undated return fee.

For a one-off fee, enter one payment in the comparison tool. Leave additional costs at zero only when the provider confirms they do not apply. A specialist case can need a separate quote even where the basic return is inexpensive.

Compare the same tax-return job

Illustrative example.

Consider an invented £120 quote that excludes a separate £60 bookkeeping tidy-up and an invented £180 quote that includes the same tidy-up. Their totals are both £180, assuming identical work and any applicable VAT are included. A headline difference has disappeared once the scope is matched.

Now suppose the client also sold a rental property. Neither price should be assumed to include a separate property-disposal report. List that event before accepting either quote, rather than expecting a routine annual return to cover every reporting task.

Actions to take
CheckPractical action
Annual returnIdentify the year and all income sources included.
Bookkeeping preparationCheck whether records must arrive reconciled or whether tidying is included.
Separate reportingAsk about disposals, historic corrections and specialist calculations.

Does a higher fee mean more tax will be saved?

A fee does not establish entitlement to a deduction or relief. Compare the work and expertise required for your facts, rather than an unverified saving promise.

What if I find another income source after paying?

Tell the accountant before approving the return. Confirm whether the extra work changes the scope or price.

  • Return year
  • Employment, business, rental and other income
  • Record condition and missing documents
  • Disposals or earlier-return corrections
  • Preparation, review and filing included in quote

title: Joining an MTD Service Mid-Year: What Happens to Earlier Quarters?
excerpt: Joining an MTD service during the tax year does not, by itself, explain what happened to earlier updates. Your new accountant needs a starting position before deciding what work remains.
metaTitle: Join an MTD Service Mid-Year: Earlier Updates | TaxSimba
metaDescription: Joining an MTD service mid-year? Prepare your earlier records and submission history, check outstanding updates and agree any catch-up work before paying.
featuredImageAlt: A business owner and accountant organise earlier receipts alongside a trail of reporting calendars.

sources.label: GOV.UK — create digital records
GOV.UK — choose agents for making tax digital for income tax

content:
You can join an MTD service during the year, but earlier records still matter. Give your new accountant the records from the tax-year start and proof of any updates already sent. Agree who will deal with outstanding updates, corrections and the annual return before the next deadline.

Find out what has already been sent

Make a short list of earlier update periods. Mark each as submitted, outstanding or uncertain, and name the person who handled it. Keep the software confirmations with the underlying records. Your recollection is helpful, but it is not the same as proof that HMRC received the update.

Give the new accountant the year so far

MTD updates are cumulative. If you join before the third update, the accountant needs the records from the tax-year start, not just the latest three months. Share exports, invoices, bank records and adjustments, including any previous corrections.

Agree the starting work and cost

Three situations need different plans: earlier updates are correct, they need correction, or they have not been sent. Ask which work your new package includes and get any catch-up charge agreed before it starts. A new subscription does not itself clear an overdue filing.

Send this with your enquiry: “I need support for 2026/27. My first two updates were filed by another accountant. I have the confirmations and records. Please confirm what you need before the next update and whether reviewing the earlier work costs extra.”

Keep the earlier annual return on the list

Your 2025/26 Self Assessment return and 2026/27 MTD work concern different years. Confirm who is finishing each one. Before buying MTD support, give TaxSimba the service year, income sources and submission history so the starting work can be agreed.

Make a handover sheet before choosing a start date

Example handover record
ItemRecord this
Business and reporting basisFor example: sole trade, standard periods, 2026/27.
Earlier workEach period, its status and the confirmation held.
Next filingThe named firm responsible and its document cut-off.
Unresolved itemsThe missing record, who obtains it and the agreed review charge.

Use one row per business. If the earlier submission status is uncertain, label it uncertain; do not guess that another firm filed it. Ask the incoming accountant to confirm acceptance of the records and next filing in writing.

Joining before the third update: a handover example

Illustrative example.

A sole trader joins a new service after two updates were sent by another accountant. The incoming accountant receives the earlier confirmations but no transaction export. Those confirmations show what was sent; they do not supply the underlying records needed to reconcile the next cumulative update.

The practical handover is therefore two-part: obtain the filing history and obtain records from the tax-year start. Agree who requests missing exports, checks the year-to-date totals and sends the next update. The example assumes standard update periods; confirm your actual accounting periods in the software.

Actions to take
CheckPractical action
Earlier updates confirmedRetain the business, period and submission evidence.
Earlier records missingRequest exports and supporting records before treating the handover as complete.
Correction identifiedAgree who corrects the records and checks the next filing outcome.

Can I start keeping records only from the joining date?

That leaves the incoming accountant without the earlier part of the tax-year picture. Arrange access to records from the start of the year.

Should I submit earlier updates again?

Check the existing filing history first. An unclear dashboard is a reason to investigate, not proof that every earlier update needs resending.

  • Joining date and next update deadline
  • Businesses and accounting periods
  • Previous submission confirmations
  • Year-to-date records and exports
  • Named owner of missing records and next filing

title: Can I Switch MTD Accountants Halfway Through the Tax Year?
excerpt: You can explore changing your MTD accountant during the year, but a good handover matters more than the date you move. The incoming accountant needs to understand both the records and the work already submitted.
metaTitle: Switch MTD Accountant Mid-Year: Handover | TaxSimba
metaDescription: Switching MTD accountants during the year? Use a handover checklist for digital records, submission history, agent permissions and the next filing deadline.
featuredImageAlt: Two accountants hand over a closed records folder while their client oversees the transfer.

sources.label: GOV.UK — choose agents for making tax digital for income tax
GOV.UK — authorising an agent to deal with your tax affairs

content:
Yes, you can change MTD accountants during the tax year. Arrange the records, HMRC permissions and next filing responsibility before the handover. Switching firms does not automatically correct old mistakes or transfer every software record.

Set a handover date and name the next filer

Before ending the old arrangement, agree which firm will send the next update and who will prepare the annual return. Put the responsibility in writing. A handover can otherwise leave both firms expecting the other to file.

Ask for records you can actually use

  • Digital bookkeeping records and a usable export.
  • Update dates, cumulative figures and submission confirmations.
  • Unanswered questions, corrections and unpaid service invoices.
  • The reporting basis already selected: standard or calendar periods.

HMRC access alone does not provide the invoices and reconciliations behind the figures. Ask how long you can access the old software and download records before that access ends.

Review HMRC permissions separately

Make sure the new accountant has permission for the jobs they will handle. Ending a contract does not automatically remove every HMRC or software permission. If another firm stays involved, clarify whether it acts as a main or supporting agent.

Do not restart the year at the moving date

The next cumulative update still needs the year-to-date records. Ask the incoming accountant to explain any extra review or correction fee before work starts. Switching firms does not automatically fix earlier errors.

For TaxSimba, provide the available export and next deadline before committing to a package. See joining an MTD service mid-year for the starting-period questions.

A handover request you can adapt

Please confirm which filings you will complete before our handover date, which remain outstanding, and how I can obtain my bookkeeping export, supporting documents and submission confirmations. Please also confirm when my access to your software ends and any fees for the handover. My next accountant needs the reporting basis and year-to-date figures.

Add your businesses and the next deadline. Copying records is only half the handover: get the incoming firm’s confirmation that it can open the export and has accepted the next job. Ask about payroll or VAT separately if the outgoing firm handles those too.

A switch with two accountants involved

Illustrative example.

A landlord appoints a new accountant while the former firm is still preparing an update. A commercial engagement letter alone does not establish who now has the appropriate HMRC permissions or who will send the work already in progress.

Write a handover note naming the owner of the next update and annual return. Match permissions to the agreed roles and obtain records and filing evidence. If the old firm will finish a specific task, record that boundary explicitly; avoid two people independently submitting the same work.

Actions to take
CheckPractical action
RecordsAgree export format, period covered and delivery date.
PermissionsCheck the relevant main or supporting-agent authorisation.
Work in progressName the person responsible for checking and sending each outstanding task.

Is cancelling the old engagement enough?

No. Commercial arrangements, access permissions and outstanding filing tasks each need attention.

What if the two firms disagree about what was filed?

Compare the submission evidence and HMRC activity before taking another filing action. Keep the resolution with the handover record.

  • Old and new accountant contact details
  • Handover date
  • Work completed and submission evidence
  • Outstanding tasks with named owners
  • Record exports and authorisation status

title: Does MTD Mean Paying Income Tax Every Quarter?
excerpt: Quarterly MTD updates are not automatically quarterly tax bills. Reporting your business information and paying your Income Tax are separate parts of the process.
metaTitle: Does MTD Mean Quarterly Income Tax Payments? | TaxSimba
metaDescription: MTD quarterly updates report your records; they are not automatically tax bills. Understand estimates, annual returns and separate Income Tax payment dates.
featuredImageAlt: A sole trader and accountant separate a reporting calendar from a savings jar used to budget for tax.

sources.label: GOV.UK — using making tax digital for income tax for the first time
GOV.UK — deadlines

content:
No. MTD quarterly updates report income and expenses; they are not quarterly Income Tax bills. Your tax payments, any payments on account and the fee you pay your accountant are separate. Check your HMRC statement for the amounts and dates you actually owe.

Three different things can appear on your screen

  • A quarterly update: business or property figures sent to HMRC.
  • An estimated tax figure: a working view that can change before the annual return is final.
  • A service invoice: the accountant or software provider’s charge.

Paying one does not settle the others. Check the payee and description before making a payment.

Which dates matter for tax payments?

The annual balancing payment is normally due by the following 31 January. Payments on account can also be due in January and July. Use your HMRC statement to see what actually applies; MTD does not turn every quarterly update into a demand for one quarter of your estimated annual tax.

For example, a November update and a November accountant’s invoice do not, by themselves, create a new November Income Tax bill. You may still want to set money aside, but savings in your bank are different from tax paid to HMRC.

Use the estimate to plan, not to guess a payment

Ask what income, reliefs and adjustments are missing from the estimate. If you have a PAYE job, rental income or other investments, the trade’s figures alone may not explain the eventual personal bill. Keep your payments-on-account schedule with the records you share with the accountant.

Label the payment before you make it

Suppose your accountant charges £40 a month and the software shows an estimated £3,600 annual tax figure. Twelve service payments of £40 total £480 paid to the provider. They do not reduce the £3,600 estimate or count as tax paid to HMRC.

Keep a simple payment list: payee, reference, amount, due date and confirmation. Use HMRC’s actual statement for tax amounts due. Do not divide the estimate by four and assume the result is a quarterly bill.

An update estimate is not a payment instruction

Illustrative example.

A fictional sole trader sees a £2,400 estimate after an update and assumes a £600 payment is due immediately because there are four quarters. That division does not establish any legal payment obligation. The estimate may change as records and other income are added.

Keep three separate records: the update sent, the current estimate and the actual amounts and dates HMRC says are payable. A savings transfer you make for budgeting is your own planning decision, not evidence of a new quarterly tax-payment deadline.

Actions to take
CheckPractical action
Quarterly updateCheck the reporting period and successful submission.
In-year estimateUse as provisional planning information, with its limitations.
Payment liabilityCheck the actual HMRC statement, payment dates and amounts.

Should I divide the estimate by four and pay that?

Not as a way of determining what is legally due. Check the actual liability and payment timetable separately.

Can I put money aside monthly?

Yes, budgeting is separate from when HMRC requires payment. Revisit your savings plan as better information becomes available.

  • Update period and confirmation
  • Date and assumptions of current estimate
  • Other income not yet reflected
  • Actual HMRC payment dates and amounts
  • Personal tax-budget review date

title: Self Assessment for 2025/26 and MTD for 2026/27: Why Both May Be Due
excerpt: Starting MTD does not remove a return due for an earlier tax year. In autumn 2026, some people are managing 2026/27 MTD work while still preparing their 2025/26 Self Assessment.
metaTitle: 2025/26 Self Assessment and 2026/27 MTD | TaxSimba
metaDescription: Starting MTD in 2026/27 does not finish your 2025/26 Self Assessment. Track both tax years, records, services and filing responsibilities separately.
featuredImageAlt: A business owner and accountant keep a completed-year folder separate from current digital records.

sources.label: GOV.UK — deadlines
GOV.UK — using making tax digital for income tax for the first time
GOV.UK — submit your tax return

content:
Yes, both can be due because they cover different years. Your 2025/26 online Self Assessment return is normally due on 31 January 2027. Your 2026/27 MTD updates relate to the following tax year, whose annual return is due on 31 January 2028.

Put both years on one timeline

Two tax years, two sets of work
WorkPeriodUsual online annual deadline
Earlier Self Assessment return6 April 2025 to 5 April 202631 January 2027
MTD digital records and updates, then annual return6 April 2026 to 5 April 202731 January 2028

The MTD annual deadline does not move the earlier return into 2028. Specific HMRC notices can affect filing dates, so keep them with the relevant year.

What to label before sending documents

Use a separate folder for each tax year and income source. A statement downloaded in October 2026 might cover 2025/26; its download date does not decide the tax year. Give the accountant the actual transaction or statement dates where anything crosses the boundary.

Check which year your package covers

A plan including the annual return for your MTD service year does not automatically include the previous year’s separate return. Ask TaxSimba to identify both jobs and the fees. If two firms are involved, write down who finishes 2025/26 and who handles 2026/27.

Evidence that each job is done

Keep separate submission confirmations. A completed MTD update is not proof that the earlier Self Assessment return has been filed. Keep tax-payment evidence separately too: filing the figures and paying the amount due are different actions.

Keep two document requests separate

If the accountant asks for your 2025/26 P60 while also checking 2026/27 business records, both requests can be correct. Reply with the tax year in each filename and message. For example, label an employment document “P60 2025-26” and the current trade export “Trade records 6 April to 5 October 2026”.

Before approving anything, ask: which year does this submission finish? Keep a small tracker with one line for the earlier return and another for each current MTD business. A completed item in one line does not close the others.

Two tax years on the same desk

Illustrative example.

In autumn 2026, a taxpayer can be preparing the annual return for 6 April 2025 to 5 April 2026 while maintaining MTD records for 2026/27. A folder called “this year” makes it easy to mix them up.

Label documents with explicit start and end dates. Give the accountant an employment certificate for the earlier return and a separate current-year transaction export for MTD work. Completing one task does not establish that the other has been filed. Check each reporting obligation and its evidence independently.

Actions to take
CheckPractical action
2025/26 return recordsUse income and expense evidence for that tax year.
2026/27 MTD recordsMaintain the current-year digital records and update history.
Submission evidenceKeep a separate confirmation for each return or update.

Does a current MTD update finish the earlier return?

No. It covers a different reporting task and period. Confirm the earlier return position separately.

Can one accountant handle both?

Potentially, if the engagement covers both jobs and the accountant has the appropriate authority. Confirm the years and tasks in writing.

title: Are MTD Quarterly Updates Cumulative? A Simple Worked Example
excerpt: Yes. MTD quarterly updates report the tax year so far, rather than treating each submission as a separate three-month total. This distinction matters when you check what has been sent.
metaTitle: Are MTD Quarterly Updates Cumulative? | TaxSimba
metaDescription: See how cumulative MTD updates report year-to-date figures, with a £12,000 plus £15,000 example and checks to avoid counting earlier income twice.
featuredImageAlt: An accountant and client organise a growing sequence of records to illustrate cumulative reporting.

sources.label: GOV.UK — send quarterly updates

content:
Yes. Each MTD update covers the tax year so far. If income is £12,000 in the first period and £15,000 in the second, the second update reports £27,000 of cumulative income—not another standalone £15,000. Expenses must also reflect the correct year-to-date records.

Quarterly activity and submitted totals are different

Illustrative income-only example
UpdateNew income in the periodCumulative income submitted
First£12,000£12,000
Second£15,000£27,000
Third£9,000£36,000

Do not add £12,000, £27,000 and £36,000 to find annual income. That would count earlier activity more than once. The example leaves out expenses and is not a personal tax calculation.

Read the start date as well as the end date

For standard periods, the second update covers 6 April to 5 October. The third runs from 6 April to 5 January. Calendar periods have different coverage dates, so check which basis the software uses before comparing it with a bank export.

Why a correction can change the next update

Once an earlier transaction is corrected in the digital records, the next cumulative update needs to reflect the corrected year-to-date position. Ask the accountant which action is needed at the stage you have reached; do not assume the answer is always a separate resubmission.

Before you approve

Match the business, tax year, period and category totals to the records for the whole cumulative period. If you changed accountants, provide the earlier records as well. See correcting an MTD mistake if the figures do not reconcile.

Add expenses to the example

Suppose earlier cumulative income was £12,000 and expenses were £3,000. New-period income is £15,000 and expenses are £4,000. Before corrections, the next totals are £27,000 income and £7,000 expenses. If £240 of the earlier expenses was private and must be removed, cumulative expenses become £6,760.

The calculator below lets you change those numbers. Enter a correction only once. If the starting cumulative expenses already exclude the £240, subtracting it again would create a second mistake.

A cumulative update in numbers

Illustrative example.

Assume standard periods and one business. By 5 July, the records show £10,000 income and £3,000 expenses. From 6 July to 5 October, the business records another £8,000 income and £2,000 expenses. The second update covers the tax year so far: £18,000 income and £5,000 expenses, assuming no corrections.

Do not enter £18,000 as fresh transactions on top of the earlier £10,000. The software should build the cumulative totals from the underlying records. These figures illustrate record aggregation only; they are not a final taxable-profit or tax-bill calculation.

Actions to take
CheckPractical action
First update: 6 April–5 JulyIncome £10,000; expenses £3,000.
Additional records: 6 July–5 OctoberIncome £8,000; expenses £2,000.
Second update: 6 April–5 OctoberIncome £18,000; expenses £5,000.

Do I add the first two submitted totals together?

That would count the first period twice. Compare underlying records and the cumulative period covered by each update.

What if I use calendar update periods?

Confirm the elected periods in your software. This example uses standard periods and should not be copied without checking the period settings.

title: Found a Mistake After an MTD Update? How to Prepare for a Correction
excerpt: Finding an omitted receipt or wrongly categorised transaction after an MTD update does not mean you should start deleting submissions. First identify what needs correcting in the underlying records.
metaTitle: Correct an MTD Quarterly Update: Next Steps | TaxSimba
metaDescription: Found an error after an MTD update? Gather the evidence, correct the underlying records and check the filing stage before choosing the correction process.
featuredImageAlt: A client spots a receipt in the wrong pile and an accountant moves it to the correct records folder.

sources.label: GOV.UK — create digital records
GOV.UK — adjust your self employment and property income
GOV.UK — Submit and amend your MTD tax return

content:
Tell your accountant exactly which transaction is wrong and correct the digital records. HMRC’s next step depends on whether further updates or the annual return have already been sent. Avoid filing a duplicate or changing several copies of the records independently.

Send one clear description of the error

Include the date, amount, business, record and supporting document. Say whether the issue is missing income, a duplicate, an expense in the wrong category or private spending included by mistake.

For example: “The £240 payment on 12 September was personal, but it appears in business expenses. Here is the receipt and bank reference. Please check the records and whether any filing needs changing.”

Correction route by stage
Where you areWhat to do
More updates remain in the yearCorrect the digital records promptly. The next cumulative update includes the correction.
Fourth update sent; annual return not filedCorrect the records and resend the fourth update, or adjust the category total in software and reflect that change in the digital records. Agree the route with your agent.
Annual return already submittedUse compatible software to amend the return; the normal window is 12 months from its submission deadline. Check the relevant route if that window has closed.

Follow HMRC’s digital-record correction guidance and its annual-return amendment guidance. Keep the original evidence and correction explanation. The calculator illustrates totals; it does not send a correction.

Confirm the work before any extra fee

If reviewing earlier records is outside the package, ask what work is proposed and agree the price first. Payment for a correction is not proof that HMRC’s figures have changed. Ask for confirmation of the actual correction or submission.

If an annual return has already been filed

Raise the issue promptly and use the relevant amendment route. Changing a local spreadsheet alone does not change a filed return. See amending a Self Assessment return for the ordinary amendment window, and give your accountant the exact year and filing history.

A duplicate receipt discovered after filing

Illustrative example.

Suppose a first update included the same £200 business receipt twice. At the next update, the unreconciled records would show £7,000 of year-to-date expenses. Correcting the duplicate reduces those records to £6,800, assuming nothing else changes. Keep the receipt and an explanation of the removal.

This is a bookkeeping correction example, not a tax adjustment or instruction to amend an annual return. The filing action depends on the stage of the year and what has already been submitted. After the final quarterly update or annual return, check the applicable correction route rather than assuming a later routine update will resolve it.

Actions to take
CheckPractical action
Duplicate recordIdentify the two entries and the one underlying receipt.
Corrected recordsRemove the duplication without losing the evidence trail.
Filing stageCheck whether a further update or a different correction process is needed.

Should I delete the supporting receipt?

No. Keep evidence of the genuine cost and the reason a duplicate record was removed.

What if the annual return is already submitted?

Tell the accountant which return was filed and when. An annual-return correction is a separate procedural check.

title: Waiting for a UTR Before January? Steps to Take While You Wait
excerpt: Waiting for a Unique Taxpayer Reference is a reason to act early, not a reason to leave every other part of the return until later. Registration and preparing your tax information can involve separate tasks.
metaTitle: Waiting for a UTR? Prepare Your Tax Return | TaxSimba
metaDescription: Waiting for a UTR before January? Check registration, gather your tax-year records and tell your accountant about deadlines while the reference is resolved.
featuredImageAlt: A freelancer checks for a letter while keeping tax-return records organised at a home-office desk.

sources.label: GOV.UK — register for self assessment
GOV.UK — deadlines
GOV.UK — Find your UTR number
GOV.UK — Check when to expect an HMRC reply
GOV.UK — Self Assessment enquiries

content:
Look for an existing UTR in your HMRC account, app or earlier correspondence before applying again. If you are waiting after registration, keep the acknowledgement and prepare your records now. A missing reference does not automatically postpone tax payment; follow any filing deadline HMRC gives you.

Check whether a UTR already exists

HMRC’s Find your UTR page explains where to look, including your online account, the HMRC app and earlier Self Assessment correspondence. If you filed years ago, finding or reactivating the existing record may be the right step. Repeated new applications can add confusion.

If you have registered and are waiting

Keep the application date and acknowledgement. Use the current official registration guidance to check progress or contact HMRC; avoid a delivery promise copied from an old article. Tell the accountant the tax year and any notice deadline as well as the missing reference.

Prepare everything else now

Gather PAYE records, business or rental statements, expense evidence and other income details. Note missing documents. You can answer questions and prepare the return while the reference issue is being resolved. TaxSimba onboarding access does not itself confirm that HMRC references and agent permissions are ready for filing.

Read the actual filing notice

A missing UTR does not automatically extend the deadline. Where you register after 5 October 2026, HMRC says it gives a filing deadline three months from the date of its letter or email. The tax-payment deadline remains 31 January 2027. Follow the notice that applies to you and raise any uncertainty promptly.

Share the acknowledgement securely with the accountant. Keep your Government Gateway password and one-time codes private.

If the reference still cannot be found

  1. For a new application, enter the registration details in HMRC’s reply-time checker.
  2. If the expected date has passed, or an existing UTR cannot be retrieved, use Self Assessment enquiries.
  3. Keep the enquiry date, acknowledgement and any response with your filing notice. Tell the accountant what remains unresolved.

Use your individual Self Assessment UTR. A limited company’s Corporation Tax UTR is a different reference. Resolve the reference problem while preparing the figures rather than delaying both jobs.

Waiting for a UTR without losing preparation time

Illustrative example.

A first-time filer is waiting for their UTR while the usual January deadline approaches. They can still reconcile business records, collect employment evidence and retain proof of registration. Waiting does not make those preparation tasks impossible.

If registration took place after 5 October, check the actual HMRC letter: the filing deadline may differ. A later filing deadline does not automatically move the payment deadline. Share the letter and registration evidence with the accountant so the filing and payment positions are checked separately.

Actions to take
CheckPractical action
Registration evidenceKeep the date, acknowledgement and correspondence.
Return preparationOrganise the tax-year figures while waiting for access details.
Deadline uncertaintyRead the HMRC notice and check filing and payment separately.

Does paying for an accountant speed up HMRC issuing a UTR?

Do not assume a provider can control HMRC processing. Ask what preparation can proceed and what requires the reference.

Can I use a different reference number?

Do not substitute a National Insurance number or another identifier for a UTR where a UTR is required. Check the official process.

title: Employed and Self-Employed: What Your Accountant Needs for One Tax Return
excerpt: A job and a self-employed activity can belong in the same individual tax return. The accountant needs both sets of information to assess the complete position rather than treating the side business in isolation.
metaTitle: Employed and Self-Employed Tax Return Records | TaxSimba
metaDescription: Prepare one tax return for employment and self-employment: gather PAYE documents, business records and other income details for the correct tax year.
featuredImageAlt: An employee with a side business and an accountant combine two sets of records into one tax-return folder.

sources.label: GOV.UK — check if you need tax return
GOV.UK — what records to keep

content:
Employment and self-employment are normally reported together in one personal tax return when a return is required. Give the accountant your PAYE documents and your business records so income, expenses and tax already deducted are included once. You do not get a separate Personal Allowance for each activity.

Bring the PAYE figures as well as the business accounts

Provide your P60 or relevant P45, taxable-benefit information and details of job changes. PAYE tax already deducted matters to the final calculation. Sending only the side-business receipts can leave the return incomplete.

Keep the business trail separate

Collect sales, allowable costs, invoices and the trading start or stop date. Mark money transferred from your salary account as a transfer, rather than another customer sale. Costs paid personally still need evidence if they relate to the trade.

There is one overall personal tax position

You do not receive a fresh Personal Allowance for each job or trade. The return brings relevant income together and accounts for tax already paid. Tell the accountant about property, pensions, investment income and student or postgraduate loans too.

Check whether a return is required

A genuine sole trade with gross receipts over £1,000 normally triggers a return, but other circumstances and HMRC notices also matter. Use the current official checker rather than assuming every small side payment creates the same obligation.

Before choosing an SA package, describe all income sources and the year. This makes it easier to confirm the right work and avoid discovering an unquoted extra calculation just before filing.

Reconcile the side business without counting your wages twice

Suppose £500 moves from your salary account to your business account to pay a supplier. That transfer is not another £500 customer sale. Keep the transfer identifiable and give the accountant the supplier invoice separately.

Make a two-part cover sheet: employment documents and tax deducted on one side; business income, costs and accounting period on the other. Add any other income below it. This helps the accountant distinguish the source of funds from the income being taxed.

One return, two kinds of income evidence

Illustrative example.

A fictional employee has £28,000 of PAYE employment income and a side business with £9,000 income and £2,000 expenses. Bring all three figures, the employment tax deducted and the business evidence. Do not report only the £9,000 paid through the business account.

The £7,000 difference between business income and expenses is only a simplified starting figure in this example. It does not calculate the final tax due, allowances, adjustments or National Insurance. PAYE tax already deducted is evidence to reconcile, not a reason to leave employment off the return.

Actions to take
CheckPractical action
EmploymentP60/P45, relevant benefits and tax already deducted.
Side businessSales records, expenses, private-use explanations and accounting method.
Overall positionOther income and relevant contributions or repayments for review.

Should I subtract PAYE deductions from business sales?

No. Keep employment income, employment tax and business records as separate inputs for the return.

What if I changed jobs?

Provide documents for the relevant employments and explain changes so the accountant can reconcile the tax-year position.

  • PAYE tax deducted and benefits
  • Business income and expense records

title: Uber and Private-Hire Driver Tax Returns: A Record-Keeping Checklist
excerpt: For a self-employed private-hire driver, the amount paid into the bank may not tell the full story. Platform deductions and different payment methods can make a tax return harder to prepare from bank statements alone.
metaTitle: Uber & Private-Hire Driver Tax Return Checklist | TaxSimba
metaDescription: Prepare your Uber or private-hire driver tax return with platform statements, mileage records and vehicle costs. Avoid confusing net payouts with income.
featuredImageAlt: A private-hire driver and accountant compare earnings statements, mileage records and vehicle receipts.

sources.label: GOV.UK — travel
GOV.UK — vehicles
GOV.UK — what records to keep

content:
For a private-hire driver’s return, keep the full platform earnings statements, fees, cash fares and vehicle records. Net bank payouts alone can miss income and charges. The vehicle method and private use affect what you can claim, so keep mileage and purchase or lease details together.

Download gross earnings, not just payouts

Keep statements from every platform and any direct bookings. Record fares, cash receipts, tips, refunds and platform fees where relevant. A payout after commission is not automatically the gross sales figure.

Illustration: fares of £1,000 less a £200 platform fee produce an £800 payout. If the records show only £800 of sales and then deduct £200 again, they understate the result. Reconcile the fee separately and check adjustments against the actual statement.

Build a driver-specific expense folder

  • Vehicle purchase, lease or finance agreement.
  • Business-mile records and previous vehicle claims.
  • Insurance, servicing and other vehicle invoices.
  • Platform charges, licensing and other work costs for review.
  • Phone bills and a clear explanation of private use.

Having an invoice does not automatically make every cost deductible. Fines and private driving are not business expenses. Whether a particular journey qualifies depends on the working pattern.

Choose the vehicle method consistently

Simplified mileage and actual running costs are alternatives for the costs they cover. Do not add fuel and servicing to the same mileage claim. Prior claims and the vehicle type can affect the available method, so supply the history before the accountant calculates it.

Explain how you work

Private-hire arrangements can raise employment-status questions. Say who pays you, how bookings work and whether you have another job. Use the vehicle-records guide and send the complete income picture when arranging TaxSimba support.

Before comparing mileage with actual vehicle costs

Identify the vehicle type and previous claims first. HMRC excludes certain commercially designed vehicles, including black cabs, from simplified mileage. Prior capital-allowance or purchase-expense claims can also prevent its use. A private-hire car is not automatically treated the same as every taxi.

Keep a dated business-mile log alongside actual running costs so an eligible comparison can be made. The tax year matters: HMRC lists 45p for the first 10,000 qualifying car or goods-vehicle miles before 6 April 2026, rising to 55p for 2026/27. The rate above 10,000 remains 25p. Check the linked mileage guide before using a rate.

Why a driver’s bank deposit may differ from earnings

Illustrative example.

Assume a fictional platform statement shows £1,000 gross fares, a £200 platform fee and an £800 payout, with no other adjustments. The payout alone is not the complete earnings picture. Record and reconcile the statement on the accounting basis that applies.

Do not start with £800 as sales and then deduct the same £200 fee again. Cash fares, tips, refunds or amounts handled outside the platform can add further reconciliation items. This simplified illustration does not decide employment status, VAT treatment or the deductibility of every charge.

Actions to take
CheckPractical action
Gross fares in the example£1,000 before the stated platform fee.
Platform fee in the example£200 shown separately, subject to the correct treatment.
Bank payout in the example£800 to reconcile, not a second set of sales.

Does every difference mean a missing expense?

No. Timing, refunds, adjustments and different payment routes can all affect the reconciliation. Obtain the statement breakdown.

Can a bank statement replace the mileage record?

A bank statement shows payments, not the business journeys travelled. Keep the relevant journey evidence separately.

title: Deliveroo, Uber Eats and Courier Tax Returns: Getting Your Records Ready
excerpt: Working across delivery apps can leave your tax information scattered between weekly statements, cash records and bank deposits. Organising it by platform is a useful first step towards a complete return.
metaTitle: Delivery Driver & Courier Tax Return Records | TaxSimba
metaDescription: Get your Deliveroo, Uber Eats or courier tax records ready: collect all platform statements, reconcile payouts and organise vehicle and work expenses.
featuredImageAlt: A bicycle delivery courier and accountant organise platform statements, work receipts and a mileage notebook.

sources.label: GOV.UK — selling goods or services on a digital platform
GOV.UK — travel
GOV.UK — office property

content:
Keep earnings and fee statements from every delivery app, plus direct bookings, tips and relevant costs. Reconcile the full earnings to the payouts. Platform deductions are not automatically tax, and a platform sending data to HMRC does not complete your personal return.

Reconcile every app separately

Download the full earnings and fee statements from each platform. Add cash tips and direct work where applicable. Reconcile fees, refunds and adjustments to the bank payout before combining the year’s income.

Illustration: one app shows £600 earnings and £60 fees, paying £540. Another pays £300 with no deductions shown. The first statement still needs its gross earnings and fee identified; adding bank deposits alone gives a different picture from the underlying activity.

Tell the accountant what you ride or drive

A bicycle, motorcycle and car do not automatically use the same expense treatment. Keep purchase or lease records, relevant insurance and business-mile evidence. Record when you changed vehicle and how much private use there was.

Do not mistake app charges for tax

A net payout can reflect a platform fee rather than Income Tax withheld. Read the statement rather than assuming the platform has paid your personal tax. Reporting data to HMRC is also different from filing your return.

Include the work outside the busiest app

Give the accountant other employment, private bookings and separate business records. Use the UK tax year, even if the platform summary uses a calendar year. Send any missing-period questions early so the return does not rely on one incomplete annual total.

Make the platform totals agree before combining them

Create one line per app with gross earnings, refunds, fees, other adjustments and net payout. Add the lines only after each reconciles. Keep a separate list for cash tips and direct bookings that never appeared on an app.

For example, if an app’s annual summary covers January to December, mark which months belong in each UK tax year. Do not add it to an April-to-April export of the same earnings. The same delivery must appear once, even where several reports describe it.

Two delivery apps, one complete record

Illustrative example.

Imagine App A shows £700 gross earnings and £100 fees, while App B shows £500 earnings and £50 fees. With no other adjustments, the bank payouts total £1,050, while gross earnings total £1,200 and the listed fees total £150. Keep each platform breakdown.

If the courier also received £80 from direct bookings, add those records to the reconciliation. Do not use a platform’s calendar-year report as though it automatically covers the UK tax year. These are simplified bookkeeping figures; the treatment of each amount still needs checking.

Actions to take
CheckPractical action
App A£700 earnings less £100 fees gives £600 payout.
App B£500 earnings less £50 fees gives £450 payout.
Other workDirect bookings and other receipts need separate records.

Can I send only the busiest app’s summary?

That omits other work. Include all platforms and direct customers for the relevant period.

What if a report covers January to December?

Identify its reporting dates and obtain records that allow the correct tax-year period to be prepared.

title: MTD Software or an Accountant-Managed Service: Which Do You Need?
excerpt: Buying MTD software gives you a tool. An accountant-managed service also provides professional work. The right choice depends on what you can confidently do yourself and what you want someone else to handle.
metaTitle: MTD Software vs Accountant-Managed Service | TaxSimba
metaDescription: Compare MTD software with an accountant-managed service. Check who keeps records, reviews figures, sends updates and prepares your annual tax return.
featuredImageAlt: A sole trader compares a laptop ledger with the record-keeping and filing work explained by an accountant.

sources.label: GOV.UK — choose the right software for making tax digital for income tax
GOV.UK — authorising an agent to deal with your tax affairs

content:
Choose software alone if you want to keep the records and handle the reporting yourself. Choose accountant support if you want agreed checking, bookkeeping or filing work. Compare who does each task; an MTD software subscription does not automatically include an accountant-managed return.

Compare who does the work

Three common ways to arrange MTD support
ArrangementYou doProvider does
Self-service softwareKeep/check the records and manage reportingProvide the software and advertised support
Accountant review and filingMaintain the agreed records and answer questionsReview and submit the agreed work
Managed bookkeeping and filingSupply complete evidence and review questions/figuresMaintain books and handle the work included in the engagement

These are arrangements to compare, not standard definitions every provider follows. Ask who handles each row of work in your actual quote.

Choose around your available time

If you are comfortable recording and reconciling transactions, software alone may be enough. If you prefer to supply statements and invoices and have the books maintained for you, compare managed services. Neither approach can identify every unrecorded cash sale or private payment without your input.

Check the income sources and annual return

Confirm support for every trade and relevant property source, the chosen update periods and the annual return. Ask whether earlier records or corrections cost extra. A product being MTD-compatible does not mean its entry-level plan includes unlimited bookkeeping or specialist tax advice.

Where TaxSimba fits

TaxSimba is accountant-led. Read the current package description to see which record-keeping, review and filing jobs are included. Choose the division of work you want first, then compare the full price.

Test the service with one real month

Before choosing, describe a typical month: cash sales, card settlements, expenses, missing receipts and any property income. Ask who handles each item and what you must approve. A demo showing a connected bank account does not explain who reconciles the books or resolves a doubtful expense.

Ask TaxSimba for the responsibilities confirmed in your engagement. In particular, check whether bookkeeping is done for you or whether you supply records ready for review. Keep the answer beside the price so the package matches the amount of work you can realistically do.

Choose a working arrangement, not just a product

Illustrative example.

A landlord is comfortable collecting receipts but does not want to reconcile transactions or prepare updates. A software-only subscription may provide tools without supplying that work. A managed quote might include it, but the written scope must say so.

Compare the same list of tasks across each arrangement. Ask who resolves an unexplained transfer, checks incomplete rental statements and confirms submission. Calling a service “supported” does not by itself identify the person responsible for every task.

CheckPractical action
Software onlyCheck which record-keeping and filing tasks you must complete.
Records kept by you, filing helpAgree review boundaries and the condition your records must arrive in.
Managed records and filingConfirm covered sources, query handling, submissions and exclusions.

Does software automatically check every tax judgement?

Do not assume so. Match its capabilities to your circumstances and identify the judgements you or an adviser must make.

Is “accountant support” the same as managed bookkeeping?

Not necessarily. Ask for the actual tasks, limits and responsibilities included in the engagement.

title: Authorising Your MTD Accountant Without Sharing Your Password
excerpt: Your accountant needs the appropriate authority to act for you, not a casual message containing your Government Gateway password. The authorisation should match the tax service and work being undertaken.
metaTitle: Authorise Your MTD Accountant Safely | TaxSimba
metaDescription: Authorise an MTD accountant through the appropriate HMRC process. Check the firm and permissions, keep passwords private and understand your responsibilities.
featuredImageAlt: A client uses his own laptop while an accountant explains a secure agent-authorisation request.

sources.label: GOV.UK — authorising an agent to deal with your tax affairs
GOV.UK — choose agents for making tax digital for income tax
GOV.UK — Existing client authorisations for MTD

content:
Authorise your accountant through the official HMRC process for the work they will do. Keep your Government Gateway password and security codes private. For MTD, confirm whether the accountant needs a main or supporting-agent role, especially if another firm remains involved.

Check the firm and the permission requested

Use HMRC’s official agent-authorisation process for the service concerned. Read the request and confirm the accountant’s identity through a contact method you already trust. An urgent message is not a reason to approve unexpected access.

Main and supporting agents have different roles

For MTD, the main-agent role includes finalising the overall tax position and annual return. Supporting agents can undertake the work their permissions allow, but cannot submit that annual return. If a bookkeeper and tax accountant are both involved, agree their roles before changing access.

Keep passwords and one-time codes private

Complete your own part of the official process. Do not send your Government Gateway password, security code or recovery details through email or chat. If you cannot complete the suggested route, ask about an approved alternative.

An engagement letter is a different step

The engagement records the work and terms you agree. HMRC authorisation gives permission to act through the relevant service. Signing one is not proof that the other has been completed.

You remain responsible for the information supplied for tax. Review the return before submission and keep the authorisation and engagement records. When an arrangement ends, check both outstanding filings and removal or replacement of access.

Complete the permission step and check the result

  1. Confirm whether the firm is asking to act as a main or supporting agent.
  2. For a new digital request, read the HMRC consent statement and complete your part yourself through the official journey.
  3. Ask the firm to confirm authorisation is in place for the relevant work. Then check separately that MTD signup and software access are ready.

Some existing Self Assessment permissions can be added to the agent’s services account instead of a new digital request. The firm should identify the route that applies. HMRC authorisation does not itself prove the next update has been filed.

An urgent authorisation message: what to verify

Illustrative example.

A client receives an unexpected message asking for a one-time login code to “finish accountant setup”. Instead of replying with the code, they contact the firm through the number already in their engagement records and confirm the proper authorisation route.

The same check applies to a genuine-looking request from a different firm name. Verify the organisation and the requested service before approving access. The goal is to establish the agreed authority, not to transfer control of the client’s personal sign-in credentials.

Actions to take
CheckPractical action
Known firm, expected requestCheck that the tax service and requested role match the engagement.
Unexpected sender or roleConfirm through a previously known contact channel.
Password or one-time-code requestKeep credentials private; use the official authorisation process.

Does signing a client-care letter grant HMRC access?

It records the engagement. Check the separate HMRC authorisation step rather than assuming it happened automatically.

Can a supporting agent file the annual return?

That is a main-agent responsibility under the MTD agent-role guidance. Agree who will perform it.

title: Several Years of Unfiled Tax Returns: How to Put Them in Order
excerpt: If several returns are missing, start by identifying each affected tax year and what HMRC has asked you to file. A clear year-by-year record is more useful than submitting the latest return and hoping the earlier years disappear.
metaTitle: Several Overdue Self Assessment Returns: Next Steps | TaxSimba
metaDescription: Missing several Self Assessment returns? Organise records by tax year, distinguish overdue filings from disclosures and agree the work needed to get up to date.
featuredImageAlt: A taxpayer and accountant sort older paperwork into separate tax-year folders with a clear timeline.

sources.label: HMRC / GOV.UK — deadlines
HMRC / GOV.UK — corrections
HMRC / GOV.UK — let property campaign your guide to making a disclosure

content:
Start with a list of the missing tax years and every HMRC notice. Keep records separate for each year. An outstanding return, an error in a filed return and undeclared income can need different routes, so agree the filing or disclosure plan before submitting figures.

Build a year-by-year list

For each year, record the income sources, HMRC notice, whether anything was filed and which documents are missing. A current return does not automatically settle older years. Keep the notices because they can affect the route and deadline.

Separate three different jobs

  • A missing return HMRC issued: establish how that year can be filed.
  • A filed return with an error: check the amendment window or later correction route.
  • Income never declared: check whether an official disclosure process applies.

For rental income, the Let Property Campaign guide explains a possible disclosure route. It is not a substitute for deciding which years belong on ordinary returns.

Reconstruct the records without copying guesses

Collect bank records, PAYE documents, rental statements, invoices and earlier accountant workings. Mark uncertainty. An invoice date and payment date can fall in different years, so the accounting method matters.

Agree the full work and payment plan

Tax, interest, penalties and payments on account can all affect what is owed. Filing does not automatically cancel a penalty or arrange instalments. Discuss payment difficulty while the figures are established. Ask TaxSimba whether the historic or disclosure work is accepted and get the years, scope and fee agreed before buying a routine current-year service.

Use a recovery table instead of one mixed folder

Historic-return recovery plan
YearFiling positionEvidence gapNext action
2023/24Return status to confirmMissing bank periodObtain statement and check HMRC notice.
2024/25Filed, possible errorOmitted income statementCheck correction route and deadline.
2025/26Current return to prepareP60 still neededRequest document while older work is reviewed.

This is a planning example, not a recommendation to use the same route for each year. Add the HMRC references and person responsible in your own private copy. An urgent current deadline can need attention while the older years are being reconstructed.

Build a year-by-year recovery plan

Illustrative example.

A taxpayer has an unfiled return for one year, an error in a return already filed for another, and rental income never reported for an earlier period. Labelling all three “late returns” can lead to the wrong process being used.

Create a separate line for each year, describing what HMRC requested, what was submitted and what is missing. The accountant can then distinguish preparation, correction and potential disclosure work. The order of work should reflect actual notices and deadlines, not an assumption that the newest year always comes first.

Actions to take
CheckPractical action
Return requested but missingIdentify the notice, year and outstanding filing task.
Return filed with an errorCheck the correction route and relevant time limits.
Income never reportedAsk whether a disclosure process is appropriate for the facts.

Should I copy the newest year’s figures into older returns?

No. Each year needs its own evidence and the appropriate accounting treatment. Repeated estimates can create further errors.

Does filing settle every charge automatically?

Check the resulting tax, interest, penalties and payment position separately. An appeal or payment arrangement is another task.

title: Appealing a Self Assessment Penalty: Evidence, Deadlines and Next Steps
excerpt: You may be able to challenge a Self Assessment penalty, but an appeal needs the right grounds and supporting facts. Start with the penalty notice and keep the filing or payment obligation separate from the appeal itself.
metaTitle: Appeal a Self Assessment Penalty: Evidence & Deadlines | TaxSimba
metaDescription: Check how to appeal a Self Assessment penalty: read the notice, prepare dated evidence and explain your timeline. Appeals are usually due within 30 days.
featuredImageAlt: A taxpayer and accountant compare a penalty notice, calendar and dated evidence to build an appeal timeline.

sources.label: HMRC / GOV.UK — check when to appeal a self assessment penalty for late filing or late payment
HMRC / GOV.UK — reasonable excuses
HMRC / GOV.UK — tax appeals
GOV.UK — Disagree with a penalty

content:
Read the penalty notice and its appeal instructions promptly. Appeals are normally due within 30 days. Explain what prevented you meeting the deadline, give relevant dated evidence and say what you did once the problem ended. Appealing does not file a missing return or pay the tax.

Read the notice before drafting the appeal

Identify the tax year, type of penalty, issue date and reason. Check the appeal instructions and normal 30-day window. If the return was not required, asking HMRC to withdraw the filing requirement can be a different route from arguing a reasonable excuse.

Explain what happened and when

A useful explanation connects the event to the missed deadline. Set out the dates, why it prevented compliance, when it ended and what you did afterwards. Serious illness, bereavement or a service failure needs the relevant facts; the label alone does not establish the outcome.

A short structure is: “The deadline was [date]. [Event] prevented filing from [date] to [date]. I filed on [date] after it ended. I enclose [relevant evidence].” Use only true facts. An example structure is not a promise that the excuse qualifies.

Keep the evidence relevant

Include the notice, dated correspondence and evidence that supports the actual period. Avoid unnecessary medical or other private details. A general outage screenshot from weeks later may not explain a failed attempt at the deadline.

Deal with the missing return or tax too

An appeal does not submit the return, settle tax or automatically stop every charge. If the appeal is late, explain that delay separately. Ask TaxSimba to confirm whether appeal support is available within the engagement or needs separate work; cancellation cannot be promised in advance.

Use HMRC’s appeal route for the actual penalty

HMRC’s Self Assessment appeal checker directs you to the applicable online route or forms SA370 and SA371. Follow the notice and keep proof of sending the appeal.

Record the penalty issue date immediately. HMRC normally allows 30 days from issue to contact it or appeal; explain any late appeal separately. Track the appeal, the return and the unpaid tax as separate tasks so sending a letter does not leave the original problem unresolved.

Show how the event affected the deadline

Illustrative example.

For a fictional unexpected hospital admission, a useful timeline would record the obligation’s deadline, the admission and discharge dates, why the illness prevented compliance, and when filing resumed. A letter showing an admission months away from the deadline would need further explanation.

Use only genuine evidence and relevant facts. The example illustrates how to organise an appeal, not a prediction that HMRC will accept it. If the appeal itself is late, explain that delay separately from the original missed obligation.

Actions to take
CheckPractical action
ObligationIdentify the return or payment and actual deadline.
Preventing eventExplain the dated facts and connection to non-compliance.
Recovery actionRecord what happened when the obstacle ended.

Is saying “personal difficulties” enough?

Explain the actual event, dates and effect on the obligation. A label alone does not establish the grounds.

Does an appeal mean I can ignore the notice?

No. Read the notice and check payment, interest and the underlying filing position while the appeal is considered.

title: Sold a Rental Property? Check the 60-Day Capital Gains Tax Deadline
excerpt: Selling a rental property can create a reporting obligation before the ordinary annual tax-return deadline. Waiting until January to tell the accountant may be too late for a separate property report.
metaTitle: Sold a Rental Property? Check the 60-Day CGT Deadline | TaxSimba
metaDescription: Sold a UK rental property? Check whether Capital Gains Tax must be reported and paid within 60 days of completion, and what records your accountant needs.
featuredImageAlt: A landlord and accountant review property completion papers and keys beside a calendar and an hourglass.

sources.label: GOV.UK — if you sold a property in the uk on or after 6 april 2020
GOV.UK — reporting and paying capital gains tax

content:
For a UK resident selling UK residential property, Capital Gains Tax due on the sale generally has to be reported and paid within 60 days of completion. Non-residents have wider reporting rules. Tell the accountant the completion date immediately; the annual return deadline may be too late.

The completion date starts the urgent check

Tell the accountant when the sale completes, even if the full cost paperwork is not ready. For a UK resident disposing of UK residential property with Capital Gains Tax due, the reporting and payment deadline is generally 60 days from completion. Check non-resident reporting separately because it can apply more widely.

The mortgage balance is not the gain

The amount left in your bank after repaying a mortgage is not the tax calculation. Gather the purchase and sale statements, relevant costs, ownership shares and any relief information. Financing and capital gain are different calculations.

Prepare the property’s history

  • Purchase, sale and completion dates.
  • Periods it was your home, let or used differently.
  • Changes in ownership and residence abroad.
  • Evidence of qualifying improvements and transaction costs.

Give real dates rather than “a few years ago”. Those facts can affect relief and reporting.

Confirm the separate report and annual return

A 60-day property report and an annual return can both be relevant. Ask who is responsible for each and whether the work is included in the fee. Do not assume a standard rental-income return package includes a property disposal calculation. Contact TaxSimba with the completion date and ask it to confirm the appropriate support.

Count from legal completion, then prepare the report

If completion is 20 October 2026, 60 calendar days later is 19 December 2026. That illustrates the date calculation only; first establish that the reporting rule applies. Use the date tool below and allow time to prepare and pay.

The official UK-property reporting route explains account setup and the information required. Where Self Assessment also applies, include the disposal there and account for tax already paid through the property report. Do not count that earlier payment twice.

Completion date starts a separate clock

Illustrative example.

In a fictional sale completed on 1 October 2026, adding 60 days gives 30 November 2026. If the disposal is within the residential-property reporting requirement, the relevant report and payment cannot simply wait for the usual annual-return timetable. The example assumes no special circumstances.

Tell the accountant immediately, even if one invoice is missing. Provide purchase and disposal details, ownership shares and occupation history so the actual reporting requirement and calculation can be checked. A mortgage settlement statement alone does not establish the gain.

Actions to take
CheckPractical action
CompletionRecord the actual date, rather than the estate-agent listing date.
Calculation inputsProvide acquisition, disposal, costs, ownership and relief information.
Separate tasksConfirm property reporting, payment and any annual-return entry.

Does each joint owner report the whole gain?

Give the accountant the ownership details. Each owner’s reporting position needs checking; do not duplicate the full proceeds as each person’s own disposal.

Can I wait until I have every document before mentioning the sale?

Alert the accountant immediately and list the missing records. That allows the deadline and next steps to be addressed promptly.

  • Completion and exchange dates
  • Purchase and sale statements
  • Ownership shares and residence history
  • Fees, improvements and relevant relief evidence
  • Property report, payment and annual-return responsibilities

title: Pay Self Assessment Through Your Tax Code: The 30 December Deadline
excerpt: Some people can have a Self Assessment bill collected through their PAYE tax code. If that is the route you want for your 2025/26 return, the online filing deadline for consideration is 30 December 2026, earlier than the usual January deadline.
metaTitle: Pay Self Assessment Through PAYE: 30 December Deadline | TaxSimba
metaDescription: Want to pay Self Assessment through your PAYE tax code? Check the under-£3,000 condition, income limits and 30 December online filing deadline.
featuredImageAlt: An employed taxpayer and accountant compare a payslip, return folder and calendar while planning tax collection.

sources.label: HMRC / GOV.UK — through your tax code

content:
You may be able to pay through PAYE if you owe less than £3,000, already pay tax through PAYE and file online by 30 December. HMRC also checks whether enough PAYE income is available. Confirm what is collected through your code and what still needs paying separately.

Check all the conditions

HMRC’s guidance requires a bill below £3,000, an existing PAYE source such as employment or a company pension, and filing by the relevant early deadline: 31 October on paper or 30 December online. You cannot make a part payment just to bring a bill of £3,000 or more under the limit.

There must be enough PAYE income

HMRC will not collect the bill this way if there is insufficient PAYE income, the resulting tax would exceed 50% of that income, or the collection would make you pay more than twice your usual tax. The bill being small is not the only test.

How collection works

If all conditions are met, HMRC normally arranges coding automatically unless you ask it not to on the return. It takes the relevant amount through salary or pension deductions over 12 months. Tell the accountant your preference before approving the return.

Check the outcome and any balance left

Filing before 30 December does not by itself prove the tax code has been changed. Read the coding notice and HMRC statement. Do not assume payments on account or every National Insurance amount are covered; HMRC has particular limits for Class 2.

For a 2025/26 return, aim to provide records well before 30 December 2026. If coding is unavailable, arrange another payment method rather than treating the amount as postponed.

What the monthly deduction could look like

An eligible £2,400 bill collected over 12 equal months would add £200 a month to PAYE deductions. This is an arithmetic example, not confirmation that HMRC will accept coding for your bill.

Check three things after filing: the coding notice, the first affected payslip or pension statement, and any amount still due directly to HMRC. If the expected change is missing, query it before relying on that collection method. Keep payments on account in a separate line on your payment plan.

A small bill is only one eligibility test

Illustrative example.

A fictional employee owes £2,900 and files online by 30 December. Being below £3,000 does not itself establish that collection through PAYE will happen: the other conditions and income limits still matter. Compare the HMRC coding outcome with the amount outstanding.

A different person owing £3,100 cannot make a £200 part payment simply to meet the under-£3,000 condition. These examples illustrate the eligibility boundary, not a personalised payment recommendation or assurance that a particular code will be issued.

Actions to take
CheckPractical action
Bill below £3,000Check the other PAYE and filing conditions too.
Bill £3,000 or aboveA part payment cannot be used just to meet this threshold.
Return submitted earlyVerify the coding outcome and amounts still payable.

Is 30 December the deadline for every online return?

It is the earlier online filing date relevant to this collection option. The ordinary filing deadline and your own notice still need checking.

What if HMRC does not collect the bill through my code?

Check what remains payable and arrange the appropriate payment route by the applicable deadline. Do not assume the balance has been deferred.
