title: Company Directors: Your Personal Tax Return Is Different from Company Filing
excerpt: A company’s accounts and Corporation Tax return are separate from a director’s personal tax position. Completing one does not automatically complete the other.
metaTitle: Company Director Personal Tax Return: What to Prepare | TaxSimba
metaDescription: Separate a director’s personal tax return from company filings. Gather salary, dividends, benefits, other income and the reason Self Assessment is needed.
featuredImageAlt: A company director separates company accounts and personal salary/dividend papers into different folders.

sources.label: GOV.UK — Director information hub: Self Assessment for directors
GOV.UK — Check if you need to send a Self Assessment tax return
GOV.UK — Employment SA102 and 2025/26 notes

content:
Company accounts and a director’s personal return are separate tasks. Directorship alone does not mean every person must file a personal return. Check the filing requirement, then provide salary, dividend and other personal-income records where a return is needed.

Check whether a personal return is needed

Being a director does not, by itself, settle every filing question. HMRC’s current director guidance explains that salary, dividends and other untaxed income need considering. Use the current Self Assessment checker and deal with any notice to file.

Tell the accountant about employment income, dividends, benefits and income outside the company. Do not rely only on the money transferred from the company bank account.

Gather the personal evidence

Provide the relevant employment documents, dividend records and information about other income. Explain any payments you do not understand rather than labelling every transfer as salary or a dividend yourself.

Ask the person preparing company records for the information needed for the personal return. Keep the tax year distinct from the company’s accounting period.

Confirm the purchased service

An individual SA package should not be assumed to include company accounts, Corporation Tax, payroll or work on directors’ loans. These need an explicit scope check before purchase.

Example: one company, two different returns

The company’s accounting period might end in December while the director’s personal tax year ends on 5 April. Documents need to be allocated to the relevant return; the company-year end is not automatically the cut-off for every personal figure.

Is every company withdrawal a dividend?

No. A transfer can have a different explanation, and distributions need appropriate records. Ask the accountant responsible for the company records to clarify the treatment rather than naming the payment after the event to suit the tax return.

Does MTD automatically apply to a director’s salary and dividends?

Do not infer MTD eligibility from the directorship alone. Relevant sole-trader or property income needs its own check. Personal Self Assessment, company filing and MTD eligibility are related administrative questions but are not interchangeable.

Next step: Tell TaxSimba you are a director and describe the personal income needing review. Ask separately about any company work, rather than assuming it is included.

Extra close-company details for 2025/26

Where the close-company director questions apply, the 2025/26 employment pages ask for the company’s name, registration number, dividends received from it and percentage shareholding. HMRC’s notes say to use the highest percentage shareholding in the year, calculated by reference to the nominal value of the shares.

Ask for the shareholding history as well as dividend vouchers. These employment-page details do not replace reporting the dividends in the relevant dividend section. Use the current SA102 form and notes; do not copy an older director questionnaire.

Ask for the director details needed this year

Illustrative preparation example.

A director’s personal return pack should not stop at a P60 and bank transfers. Check the current employment-page questions and obtain the relevant company, dividend and shareholding details where required. Keep the company tax year separate from the personal reporting year.

No. The company and director are separate taxpayers with different filings and income records.

title: Vinted and eBay: Does Selling Your Own Clothes Mean You Owe Tax?
excerpt: Selling unwanted clothes is not automatically the same as running a resale business. The activity behind the sales matters more than a social-media headline about a fixed number of listings.
metaTitle: Vinted and eBay: Personal Items or Taxable Trading? | TaxSimba
metaDescription: Selling online? Distinguish your own used possessions from trading, keep purchase and sale evidence and check valuable-item capital gains separately.
featuredImageAlt: A person sorts used personal clothes for sale while keeping a separate small trading-stock rack, distinction without labels.

sources.label: GOV.UK — Selling goods or services on a digital platform
GOV.UK — Check if you need to tell HMRC about your income from online platforms

content:
Selling your own unwanted clothes is not automatically trading. Buying stock to resell for profit is a different activity. Platform reporting thresholds are not tax allowances, and valuable possessions can raise separate capital-gains questions. Keep the evidence of what you sold and why.

Separate a clear-out from trading

Describe why you bought the items and what you do now. Selling your own used belongings can be different from regularly buying stock to resell at a profit. If your activity has changed over time, keep the dates clear.

HMRC’s platform guidance says reporting your details does not automatically mean you owe tax. Equally, a lack of a reporting notification does not prove that trading income is outside tax.

Keep evidence before you need it

Save sales summaries, purchase information and explanations of unusual transactions. If you are trading, keep records of associated costs and refunds as well as payouts. Do not delete transaction history simply because an account has closed.

Avoid treating a platform’s reporting threshold as a personal tax allowance. These are different rules and answer different questions.

Ask about valuable items separately

The tax treatment of a valuable possession may need a different review from ordinary trading income. Tell the accountant about high-value sales rather than assuming every personal item is automatically irrelevant.

Example: clearing a wardrobe versus buying stock

Selling clothes you originally bought for yourself is different from regularly sourcing items to resell. Keep enough information to explain the activity, especially if a platform statement shows a large number of transactions.

Is the platform’s reporting threshold a tax allowance?

No. Information-reporting rules and the rules for deciding taxable income serve different purposes. Do not conclude that a particular number of sales automatically makes every receipt taxable, or that staying below a platform-reporting threshold means a business is exempt.

What if I do both activities?

Separate the records of personal-item sales and trading stock, with purchase information where available. Give the accountant an explanation of each rather than subtracting an estimated personal amount from the final bank payouts.

Next step: Use HMRC’s online-income checker. If the activity looks like a business or you are unsure, explain the buying and selling pattern to TaxSimba before deciding whether a return is needed.

Keep a note of what you originally bought

Illustrative preparation example.

Separate unwanted clothes bought for your own use from items bought to resell. Keep purchase history and a short description of the activity. A platform telling HMRC about sales does not itself classify them as a trade or decide any capital-gains position.

Check: What evidence explains the purpose and history of the items sold?

Actions to take
CheckPractical action
Why and how were the items acquired?Distinguish personal use from buying or making items for resale.
Is the activity organised as a trade?Keep the pattern, intention, volume and records for a factual assessment.
Are any valuable possessions involved?Check capital-gains rules separately rather than using the trading allowance for every disposal.

Does platform reporting mean tax is automatically due?

No. Information reporting and tax liability are separate. The nature of the activity and applicable tax rules determine the result.

Does the £1,000 trading allowance apply per platform?

No. Relevant trading income is considered across activities and platforms under the allowance rules, not as a new allowance for each account.

title: Etsy Seller Tax Returns: Why Your Bank Payout Is Not the Whole Record
excerpt: An Etsy payout can combine sales, fees, refunds and adjustments. Preparing a tax return from the final bank deposit alone can make it difficult to understand what the shop earned and spent.
metaTitle: Etsy Seller Tax Returns: Reconcile Sales and Payouts | TaxSimba
metaDescription: Prepare Etsy tax records using gross sales, fees, refunds and payout reconciliations, plus materials, delivery and other business expense evidence.
featuredImageAlt: A handmade-goods seller reconciles marketplace fees, sales records, refunds and bank payouts, products nearby.

sources.label: GOV.UK — Selling goods or services on a digital platform
GOV.UK — Business records if you're self-employed: What records to keep
GOV.UK — Cash basis: Overview

content:
Start with Etsy’s full sales, fees, refunds and adjustments, then reconcile them to the bank payout. The final deposit is not necessarily your turnover. Include other selling platforms and align the records with the UK tax year rather than relying on a calendar-year total.

Download the shop statements

Keep transaction exports and relevant payment reports for the tax year. Record which periods they cover and retain supporting invoices. If your shop also sells elsewhere, give the accountant those records rather than assuming one marketplace report covers the whole business.

Reconcile before calculating profit

Ask how the sales figures relate to the payout. Fees deducted before the money reaches your bank need identifying, but should not be deducted again if they have already been accounted for in the figures used.

Refunds and cancelled orders need a clear trail. Keep a note when an adjustment relates to an earlier transaction so it can be considered correctly.

Organise costs by business purpose

Keep evidence for materials, packaging, postage and other shop-related spending. Explain any mixed personal use. The accounting treatment depends on your circumstances and method, not simply the name of the retailer on a receipt.

Platform reporting to HMRC does not replace your responsibility to establish the correct figures and filing position.

Example: the payout reconciliation

A shop may receive customer payments, issue refunds and have fees deducted before the remaining money reaches the bank. Keep a schedule linking those components. Do not treat the final payout and original sales as two separate sets of income.

What if statements use a calendar year?

Tell the accountant what period the export covers. UK tax-year preparation may need a different cut-off, so an annual platform report should not be copied into the return without checking its dates.

Do platform reports mean I no longer need my own records?

No. Your accountant still needs evidence to assess the correct figures and expenses. Download exports and invoices while access is available, and retain explanations for changes such as a shop closure or migration to another sales platform.

Next step: Give TaxSimba your marketplace exports, bank statements and cost records together. This is more useful than sending only the amount withdrawn from the platform.

A payout example you can check

Suppose a shop statement shows £1,000 of sales, £50 of refunds and £100 of fees, leaving an £850 payout. That £850 is the reconciliation result, not a complete list of tax-return inputs. Keep each component and the transaction dates, then apply the accounting method and any VAT treatment actually relevant to the shop.

Reconcile a platform reserve with the payout

Illustrative preparation example.

An Etsy report includes sales not yet paid out because money is held in reserve. Keep the report, fees, refunds and later release visible. Tell the accountant the accounting method before treating the bank deposit as the sales total.

Check: Which difference is a timing item, a fee, a refund or missing income?

Actions to take
CheckPractical action
What does each platform deduction represent?Separate fees, refunds and other adjustments using the detailed report.
Do payouts reconcile to the platform balance?Account for timing and retained funds rather than forcing every month to match exactly.
Are stock and other costs supported?Keep purchase records and confirm treatment under the accounting basis used.

Can I claim fees separately after reporting net payouts?

Avoid deducting the same fee twice. Reconcile gross figures and deductions consistently.

Do sales on another platform get a separate allowance?

No. Relevant trading receipts across platforms must be considered together under the applicable rules.

title: Airbnb and Holiday-Let Tax Returns After the Furnished Holiday Lettings Changes
excerpt: If you previously treated a property as a furnished holiday letting, do not reuse an old tax calculation without review. The special furnished holiday lettings regime ended for Income Tax from 6 April 2025.
metaTitle: Airbnb and Holiday Let Tax 2025/26: What Changed? | TaxSimba
metaDescription: Prepare Airbnb and holiday-let tax records after the Furnished Holiday Lettings regime ended: gross bookings, platform fees, ownership and transition records.
featuredImageAlt: A holiday-let host reviews property records and dated occupancy planner with adviser, small seaside cottage visible.

sources.label: GOV.UK — PIM4165 - Repeal of Furnished Holiday Lettings rules : Overview - HMRC internal manual
GOV.UK — Work out your rental income when you let property
GOV.UK — Check if you need to tell HMRC about your income from online platforms

content:
The furnished holiday lettings regime ended for Income Tax from 6 April 2025. A 2025/26 return should not simply reuse the old calculation. Give the accountant property-use dates, gross platform income, costs and any earlier allowances or losses needing review.

Tell the accountant how the property is used

Explain whether you let a room in your home, a whole property or several properties. Include ownership details, personal use and the dates of lettings. Short stays do not, by themselves, establish that the previous special rules continue.

Keep platform and property records together

Download booking statements showing amounts charged, fees, refunds and payouts. Keep invoices for property costs and identify spending that improves the property rather than simply maintains it. The accountant needs to review the substance of the work.

If you had prior-year losses, allowances or other carry-forward figures, provide the earlier return and calculations. These should not be guessed from the latest platform balance.

Check the scope of the service

Tell the accountant about overseas property, shared ownership or substantial services to guests. Different facts can require more work than an ordinary rental return, so agree the service before purchasing.

Example: the first year after the old regime

For an individual’s 2025/26 return, do not simply copy a prior-year furnished holiday lettings calculation. Bring it to the accountant as background, together with current records and details of any carry-forward figures.

Does using Airbnb make the letting tax-free?

No. A booking platform does not decide the tax treatment. Letting a furnished room in your home, operating a whole-property holiday let and providing substantial services can raise different questions.

Should I deduct the platform fee twice?

No. Check how the figures were assembled. If the statement shows net payouts, the accountant may need the gross booking and fee breakdown. Keep refunds, cancellations and personal-use periods identifiable so the final records reflect what actually happened.

Next step: Ask TaxSimba to review your letting arrangement and the relevant tax year. Bring the previous treatment as background, rather than assuming it remains correct after the rule change.

Bring the old holiday-let schedules to the new return

Illustrative preparation example.

Collect earlier capital-allowance and loss schedules alongside the 2025/26 property records. Do not simply copy the prior year’s furnished-holiday-letting calculation. Changes to the regime can make the history relevant even though the property still has the same guests.

Check: Which earlier balances and claims need review under the post-April-2025 rules?

Actions to take

Which tax year is being prepared?Separate the former regime's years from the post-abolition property-income treatment.
Are historical losses and allowances documented?Bring prior computations so transitional treatment can be checked.
Does the booking income reconcile?Supply gross bookings, cancellations, fees, payouts and private-use details.

Does listing on Airbnb determine the tax regime?

No. The property's facts and the law for the relevant year matter; a platform label does not preserve the former FHL rules.

Can I discard the old computations after the change?

No. Earlier losses, allowances and asset history may still matter. Keep them with the new year's property records.

title: Joint Rental Property on a Tax Return: Do Both Owners Report the Same Amount?
excerpt: Joint owners should not assume they can choose any rental-income split or that one owner’s return settles the other’s position. The ownership and relationship between the owners need to be understood first.
metaTitle: Joint Rental Property Tax Returns: Check Each Share | TaxSimba
metaDescription: Prepare joint-property tax figures using ownership evidence, gross rent, shared costs and each owner's personal return rather than copying the same totals.
featuredImageAlt: Joint landlords compare their actual ownership records and individual income folders with an accountant.

sources.label: GOV.UK — PIM1035 - Introduction: Jointly owned property and partnerships - HMRC internal manual
GOV.UK — Work out your rental income when you let property

content:
Joint owners cannot always choose whichever rent split produces the lowest tax. The ownership and relationship between the owners matter, with particular rules for spouses and civil partners. One person receiving the rent does not automatically make all of it that person’s income.

Explain who owns what

Give the accountant the ownership documents and describe how income has been reported previously. Spouses and civil partners can be subject to rules that differ from those applying to other co-owners. A relevant declaration may need formal evidence and timing requirements.

Do not change the reported split merely because one person pays the mortgage or receives the rent. Those facts need consideration, but do not replace a proper review.

Share the full property statement

Provide total rent, letting-agent deductions and expense evidence, then explain the amount you believe belongs to you. This allows the accountant to reconcile the property rather than relying on a single net figure.

If separate accountants handle each owner, make sure the underlying figures and assumptions are consistent. Otherwise the two returns may describe the same property differently.

Keep the engagement individual

Ask whether the purchased service covers one owner or both. Authorisations, approvals and tax payments belong to the relevant client, even where the property records overlap.

Example: rent paid into one owner’s account

The payment destination is useful evidence but does not, on its own, settle the share taxable on each owner. Give the accountant the ownership information and explain the arrangement behind the payment.

Do spouses and unrelated owners always use the same rules?

No. The relationship between owners and relevant ownership evidence can affect the treatment. Obtain advice on the actual arrangement instead of copying the split used by another landlord.

How do we prevent inconsistent returns?

Share the same complete property statement with the accountants concerned and identify the assumptions used for each person’s share. Keep a record of changes. If an error is discovered later, make sure the affected people know which figures need reviewing.

Next step: Send TaxSimba the ownership information and complete rental statements so your share can be checked before the return is prepared.

Give the accountant the ownership evidence

Illustrative preparation example.

Rent arrives in one owner’s account, but the property is jointly held. Supply the ownership documents and relationship between the owners before deciding the reporting split. An informal agreement about who spends the rent is not sufficient evidence of its tax treatment.

Check: What legal or beneficial ownership evidence supports the proposed shares?

Actions to take
CheckPractical action
Who owns the beneficial interest?Keep the ownership and income-allocation evidence, including relevant changes.
Do special spouse or civil-partner rules apply?Check the applicable default and any valid declaration rather than choosing an arbitrary split.
Can each person's figures be reconciled?Allocate income and costs consistently and retain the workings for both returns.

Do both owners report the full property's rent?

No. Establish the correct allocation for each person; duplicating the entire rent would misstate the personal returns.

Does paying all the mortgage change the ownership split?

Not automatically. Provide the ownership and borrowing arrangements for review rather than inferring tax shares from bank payments alone.

title: Landlord Repairs or Improvements: What to Send Your Accountant
excerpt: A property invoice is not automatically an expense you can deduct from rental income. Repairs and capital improvements can have different tax treatment, and the description on the invoice may not tell the whole story.
metaTitle: Landlord Repairs vs Improvements: Evidence to Keep | TaxSimba
metaDescription: Repair or capital improvement? Prepare itemised property invoices, before-and-after details and purchase history so the tax treatment can be checked.
featuredImageAlt: A landlord shows before-and-after property repair photos and invoices to an accountant, spare tap on desk.

sources.label: GOV.UK — Work out your rental income when you let property

content:
A repair maintains or restores what was there; an improvement can be capital expenditure. Real projects can contain both. Keep itemised invoices, before-and-after descriptions and the property history so the correct parts can be assessed rather than treating the whole bill as one expense.

Describe what changed

A repair generally restores something, while an improvement may add something beyond that. Give the accountant the before-and-after facts, not just a label such as “renovation”. Keep itemised invoices and explain whether several kinds of work were bundled into one bill.

For example, repairing storm damage and building a new extension are different projects. A replacement involving modern materials can need a more careful review than simply deciding that all new items are improvements.

Include the timing and property history

Explain when you bought the property, its condition at purchase and whether it was being let. Work before the first tenant or as part of a larger project may need particular attention.

Keep records even when a cost is not deducted from annual rental income. It may still be relevant to a later calculation, depending on the facts.

Do not force every invoice into one category

Ask the accountant whether parts of the work should be treated separately. A reasonable allocation needs evidence rather than a convenient percentage chosen at the end of the year.

Example: an itemised project

A single contractor invoice may include repairs, replacement items and an extension. Ask for a breakdown and explain the work, rather than entering the entire invoice under whichever category sounds most favourable.

Is a replacement always a repair?

Not automatically. The nature of the work, what was replaced and the broader circumstances need consideration. Modern materials do not by themselves answer every capital-versus-revenue question.

What if the cost is not deducted this year?

Keep the records anyway. A cost that is not an annual rental expense may be relevant to another calculation, depending on the circumstances. Do not discard invoices merely because they were excluded from this year’s rental-profit figure.

Next step: Share itemised invoices and a short description with TaxSimba before approving the property figures in your return.

Describe the job, not just the invoice label

Replacing damaged roof tiles to restore the existing roof and adding a new extension are different projects. One invoice can include repairs and improvement work, so ask for the cost breakdown. A modern equivalent replacement is not automatically an improvement merely because the old product is no longer sold. The actual work and property history matter.

Separate one building project into its real parts

Illustrative preparation example.

A contractor invoice covers repainting, replacing a broken fitting and adding an extension. Ask for the work to be itemised, with before-and-after descriptions. A single payment can contain different kinds of expenditure that should not be forced into one expense label.

Check: Can the cost of each distinct repair, replacement or improvement be evidenced?

When and why was the work done?Explain purchase condition, letting status and any wider project.
Is part of the invoice capital?Keep that evidence for the appropriate future calculation rather than forcing it into annual expenses.

Does a supplier calling work a repair settle the tax treatment?

No. The actual work and circumstances matter. Give the accountant enough detail to assess them.

Do modern replacement materials automatically mean improvement?

No. A modern equivalent can require a more nuanced assessment. Describe what changed in function, capacity and quality.

title: Savings Interest: When Do You Need to Tell HMRC or File a Return?
excerpt: Tax on savings interest does not always mean you need to purchase a Self Assessment service. Start by checking how HMRC expects your particular income to be reported.
metaTitle: Savings Interest: Self Assessment or Another Route? | TaxSimba
metaDescription: Add savings interest across accounts, check joint ownership and tax-free accounts, then confirm whether HMRC needs a return or can collect tax another way.
featuredImageAlt: A saver gathers interest statements from several banks beside a separate ISA folder and accountant.

sources.label: GOV.UK — Tax on savings interest: How you pay tax on savings interest
GOV.UK — Check how much tax you pay on dividends and interest from savings
GOV.UK — Savings interest allowances

content:
Savings interest does not always require a Self Assessment return. Add the relevant interest across accounts and check the allowance and reporting route for your circumstances. If you already file, give the accountant the required interest details even where a bank also reports them.

Add up the relevant interest

Gather annual interest statements from the accounts concerned, including accounts you closed. Use the tax year, not an arbitrary twelve-month period. Tell the accountant about joint accounts and different types of savings rather than assuming every payment has the same treatment.

HMRC’s current guidance explains the allowances and reporting routes. If you already complete Self Assessment, savings interest should be included in the return as required. People outside Self Assessment may have tax collected another way.

Do not infer the position from one bank

Several small amounts can add up, while income and tax bands can affect the calculation. An account being described as a savings account does not mean all interest is exempt. Explain any tax-free account status to the accountant.

Check before buying

Use HMRC’s guidance or ask for the filing requirement to be confirmed. If the only issue can be dealt with without a return, do not assume a full SA engagement is necessary.

Example: several accounts

If interest comes from three banks, prepare one schedule showing each institution and the relevant annual amount. Include closed accounts. Do not use only the balance shown in your main banking app.

Is all interest tax-free because I have an allowance?

Not necessarily. Allowances depend on the person’s wider position and the type of income or account. A return may need the information even where the resulting tax on some interest is nil.

If the bank reports interest, why tell the accountant?

The return still needs to be complete. Give the accountant the statements and explain any joint-account share. A change in a PAYE tax code should also be checked rather than assumed to match the correct year’s final liability.

Next step: Share the relevant interest statements and other income details with TaxSimba if you need a return or want the position reviewed within an agreed service.

Check the allowance and the reporting route separately

The Personal Savings Allowance is £1,000 for basic-rate, £500 for higher-rate and £0 for additional-rate taxpayers. Unused Personal Allowance and the starting rate for savings can also matter. Interest above an allowance can be taxable without automatically requiring a new tax return.

HMRC says savings interest over £10,000 must be reported on Self Assessment. For smaller amounts, tax can often be collected through a code or Simple Assessment; someone already filing includes the required interest on the return. Follow HMRC’s current instructions and any notice, especially where the bank information is wrong or incomplete.

Add the interest across relevant accounts

Illustrative preparation example.

Collect annual interest statements for each relevant account, including accounts outside the main bank. Keep the account type and gross interest identifiable. A bank reporting information to HMRC does not ensure the accountant has the complete figures for your return.

Check: Which accounts are included, and which interest belongs in the reporting calculation?

Actions to take
CheckPractical action
Do the figures cover the UK tax year?Use annual statements and include closed accounts.
Are any accounts joint or tax-free?Record the account type and relevant ownership share.
Is Self Assessment actually required?Check current HMRC reporting rules alongside other income and any notice to file.

Does every interest-tax bill require Self Assessment?

No. HMRC may collect tax another way depending on the facts. Check before purchasing an annual-return service solely for interest.

Can I ignore interest below an allowance when I already file?

Give the accountant the relevant statements so the return and allowance calculation can be completed correctly.

title: Working from Home When Self-Employed: Preparing an Expense Claim
excerpt: Working from home can involve allowable business costs, but the whole household bill does not become deductible. The useful starting point is a clear explanation of how the home is used for work.
metaTitle: Working from Home: Self-Employed Expense Records | TaxSimba
metaDescription: Prepare a supported working-from-home claim with household bills, working hours and mixed-use details, and compare actual costs with simplified expenses.
featuredImageAlt: A freelancer measures home workspace use with a planner, utility bills and laptop, cosy apartment setting.

sources.label: GOV.UK — Expenses if you're self-employed: Overview
GOV.UK — Expenses if you're self-employed: Office, property and equipment
GOV.UK — Simplified home-working expenses

content:
You can use actual allowable home-working costs or simplified expenses where eligible. Simplified rates depend on hours worked at home; they do not include phone and internet. Compare the permitted methods and do not claim the same household cost twice.

Gather the facts before choosing a method

Tell your accountant which activities take place at home, how much time they take and what space is used. Keep relevant bills and explain whether rooms have both business and personal use.

HMRC permits an appropriate business allocation for certain home costs. Simplified-expense rules may also be relevant. Ask which approach is suitable rather than choosing a convenient percentage without evidence.

Keep phone and internet claims separate enough to understand

A shared connection or mobile plan needs consideration of private use. Paying the bill from a business account does not by itself establish that the whole cost relates to work.

Avoid unsupported calculations

A spreadsheet showing the calculation is useful when it connects back to bills and a reasonable method. Keep the explanation with the figures so it can be reviewed next year.

If you use part of the property exclusively for business or are considering significant changes to the arrangement, ask about wider consequences before acting. A routine expense claim should not accidentally become a property-tax planning decision.

Example: a room used for work and family life

Explain the hours and nature of business use, keep the bills and show the proposed allocation. The fact that a desk is in a room does not make every household cost a business expense.

Can I add a flat-rate claim to all the actual household costs?

Do not assume the methods can be stacked. Ask which costs the chosen approach covers and what needs separate consideration. Keep phone and internet treatment clear enough to avoid duplication.

What if the working pattern changes?

Update the explanation rather than automatically carrying forward last year’s percentage. Moving home, renting a workspace or reducing hours can change the evidence behind the calculation. The accountant should be able to follow the method from records rather than reconstruct it from memory.

Next step: Send TaxSimba the relevant bills and a short description of your working pattern. Your accountant can review the allowable amount as part of the agreed work.

Compare the monthly simplified rates

HMRC’s simplified home-working rates are £10 for 25–50 business hours a month, £18 for 51–100 and £26 for 101 or more. A qualifying 60-hour month therefore uses £18, not £18 per hour. Phone and internet are outside this flat rate: assess their business share separately. Compare with allowable actual household costs without claiming both for the same cost.

Record hours as well as household costs

Illustrative preparation example.

For a representative month, note home-working hours and keep the relevant bills. Compare the eligible methods using the same period. Do not combine a simplified household-cost claim with the same actual household costs again. Phone and internet need their own assessment.

Check: What record supports the chosen method and prevents duplicate costs?

Actions to take
CheckPractical action
How is the home used for the business?Describe activities, space, hours and shared personal use.
Which calculation method fits?Compare the permitted methods using actual evidence and avoid overlapping deductions.
Has the arrangement changed?Update the basis after a move, new workspace or substantial change in working hours.

Can I claim all rent or mortgage payments because I work at home?

No. The type of cost and reasonable business allocation need checking. Loan capital repayments do not become business expenses.

Is exclusive business use always preferable?

It can have wider consequences. Explain the actual use and seek advice before making property-use decisions solely for a deduction.

  • Keep phone and internet use identifiable.
  • Document the chosen method and any changed circumstances.

title: Mileage or Actual Vehicle Costs: Which Records Does Your Accountant Need?
excerpt: Mileage and actual-cost methods are not two allowances to add together. Before preparing a vehicle claim, your accountant needs to know which method is available and what has been claimed before.
metaTitle: Self-Employed Mileage vs Actual Vehicle Costs | TaxSimba
metaDescription: Compare vehicle claim methods using journey records, purchase history and private-use details, and avoid claiming mileage plus the same running costs.
featuredImageAlt: A self-employed person compares mileage log with actual vehicle invoices and business-use notes, car outside.

sources.label: GOV.UK — Simplified expenses if you're self-employed: Vehicles
GOV.UK — Expenses if you're self-employed: Car, van and travel expenses

content:
Simplified mileage and actual vehicle costs are alternatives for the costs they cover. Keep business-mile records and previous-claim history before choosing. Do not add fuel and running costs to a mileage deduction for the same use or switch methods simply to maximise one year’s claim.

Keep both the business facts and the vehicle history

Provide the vehicle type, purchase or lease details, business use and any private use. Tell the accountant about previous capital allowances or deductions. Prior treatment can restrict simplified mileage claims.

A mileage record should show enough detail to explain the business journeys. Receipts remain useful for reviewing actual costs and other relevant expenses. Travel between home and a normal workplace needs particular care.

Do not decide from fuel spending alone

Fuel is only one part of a vehicle’s cost, and a flat-rate method is not calculated by simply reimbursing fuel receipts. The accountant should compare the relevant evidence and rules for the tax year.

If you use several vehicles, identify them separately. Avoid combining miles and costs in one total with no explanation of which vehicle was used.

Choose consistently and keep the evidence

Ask how the selected method affects later years before switching. A method that appears attractive for one period may not be freely changeable afterwards.

Example: one cost, two possible approaches

A vehicle used for business and privately needs a method that fits the rules and its history. A mileage calculation and fuel receipts may help a comparison, but they are not automatically two deductions for the same journeys.

Can I switch methods whenever the result looks better?

Do not assume so. Previous claims and rules for the vehicle can restrict the options. Give the accountant earlier calculations before changing anything.

What does a useful journey record include?

Keep dates, business purpose and mileage in a consistent form. Explain the start and end points where needed. An annual total with no supporting trail can be difficult to review, especially where normal commuting and business travel have been mixed together.

Next step: Give TaxSimba your mileage evidence, vehicle documents and previous return calculations so the treatment can be reviewed before the figures are approved.

Use the rate for the right year and vehicle

HMRC’s published simplified rates distinguish the years: for cars and goods vehicles, the first 10,000 business miles use 45p a mile before 6 April 2026 and 55p for 2026/27; miles above that use 25p. Motorcycles use 24p. Eligibility and previous claims still matter. For illustration, 8,000 eligible car miles in 2025/26 give £3,600 at 45p—not the following year’s £4,400 at 55p. Do not apply these car rates to a bicycle.

Recover last year’s vehicle method first

Illustrative preparation example.

Before comparing this year’s mileage and bills, locate the earlier vehicle claim and purchase history. A larger number from a new calculation does not establish that switching is allowed. Keep eligible business-mile records and actual costs so the permitted method can be checked.

Check: Which method is already in use for this vehicle, and which tax-year rates apply?

Actions to take
CheckPractical action
Is the journey genuinely business travel?Record purpose and route; distinguish normal commuting and personal use.
What has been claimed for this vehicle before?Provide prior expense and capital-allowance calculations before considering a switch.
Would the claim duplicate running costs?Apply the chosen method consistently and check any separately permitted items.

Can I switch methods every year to whichever is larger?

Not necessarily. The vehicle's history and the method's rules can restrict later choices. Check before changing.

Is fuel spending enough to prove business mileage?

No. Keep a journey log and business purpose. Fuel receipts alone do not establish which miles qualify.

  • Keep dated business journey logs.
  • Record private use and commuting separately.
  • Collect actual running-cost evidence.
  • Locate earlier claims and confirm the available method.

title: SA302 and Tax-Year Overview: Evidence for a Mortgage Application
excerpt: A mortgage lender may ask for a tax calculation and tax-year overview as evidence of self-employed income. These are related documents, but they are not the same thing as a bank statement or a promise that a loan will be approved.
metaTitle: SA302 and Tax-Year Overview: Mortgage Evidence | TaxSimba
metaDescription: Prepare the tax calculation and tax-year overview your lender requests, check the correct years and versions, and distinguish drafts from filed records.
featuredImageAlt: A mortgage applicant and adviser compare tax calculation and tax-year overview papers beside house keys.

sources.label: GOV.UK — Get your SA302 tax calculation
GOV.UK — Understand your Self Assessment tax bill: Tax calculation (SA302)

content:
Ask the lender which tax years and documents it accepts. An SA302 tax calculation and a tax-year overview are different records. Make sure they reflect the filed return and any amendment; obtaining them does not guarantee a mortgage offer.

Ask the lender exactly what it needs

Confirm the years, document format and any other requirements. HMRC explains how to obtain your SA302 tax calculation and tax-year overview, including where returns were filed using software.

A lender can have its own process. Do not assume a document accepted by one lender will be sufficient for every application.

Make sure the figures relate to the right return

Check your name, tax year and whether the return has been submitted or subsequently amended. If you have only draft figures, describe them accurately rather than presenting them as completed HMRC records.

Ask the accountant how the calculation relates to the return and whether an updated document is needed after a correction.

Keep tax preparation separate from borrowing advice

An accountant should prepare accurate figures based on the records, not change income to meet a mortgage target. The lender decides affordability and eligibility. Filing a return does not guarantee a mortgage or an immediate document turnaround.

Before requesting documents

Ask the lender or broker which years and formats it requires, then tell the accountant exactly what was requested. A tax calculation and a tax-year overview should not be treated as interchangeable simply because both mention the same year.

Can an accountant create documents before filing?

An accountant can explain the stage reached and may prepare draft calculations, but those should not be represented as a submitted return or HMRC-generated overview. Use accurate labels and check the lender’s requirements.

What if a return was amended?

Tell the person handling the application. The latest calculation may differ from an earlier copy. Keep the version and relevant tax year clear, and ask whether the supporting overview also needs refreshing before documents are sent.

Next step: Tell TaxSimba what the lender requested and the relevant tax years so the team can confirm the documents and work it can provide.

Start with HMRC’s document service

HMRC explains how to obtain an SA302 tax calculation and tax-year overview. If commercial software filed the return, ask the accountant how the calculation will be provided. Match the lender’s requested years and accepted document format before ordering extra work.

If you filed through HMRC, sign in and open Self Assessment, then the returns-and-payments details. If commercial software filed the return, obtain its tax calculation and the HMRC tax-year overview separately. HMRC says you cannot print the documents until 72 hours after filing; confirm the lender accepts the format you can provide.

Match mortgage evidence to the filed figures

Illustrative preparation example.

The lender requests two tax years, but the latest return was amended. Obtain the relevant tax calculations and overviews, checking the years and updated figures. A draft prepared before amendment can conflict with the HMRC record and delay the application.

Check: Do all requested documents relate to the correct years and the final filed position?

Actions to take
CheckPractical action
Which years and formats are required?Obtain the lender or broker's exact document request.
Are the return versions current?Check filing and amendment status before downloading or requesting copies.
Do calculations and overviews match?Keep names, tax years and versions consistent across the pack.

Are an SA302 and a tax-year overview interchangeable?

No. They show related but different information. Supply what the lender actually requests.

Can higher income be inserted to help a mortgage application?

No. The return must reflect supported figures. Lending goals do not justify changing the tax facts.

  • Check that relevant returns are filed.
  • Identify amendments and current calculations.
  • Obtain matching tax-year overviews.
  • Review the pack for names, years and consistency.

title: High Salary Alone: Do You Actually Need Self Assessment?
excerpt: A high salary is not a reliable stand-alone rule for deciding whether you need Self Assessment. Filing rules have changed, and the relevant tax year and other circumstances matter.
metaTitle: High Salary: Do You Need Self Assessment? | TaxSimba
metaDescription: Check current Self Assessment filing rules for high earners, review other income and deal with any HMRC notice rather than relying on old salary thresholds.
featuredImageAlt: A high-salary employee reviews a payslip and other-income checklist with an accountant, no assumption of automatic return.

sources.label: GOV.UK — Check if you need to send a Self Assessment tax return
GOV.UK — Complete your Self Assessment tax return for the last tax year

content:
High PAYE salary alone is not a blanket reason to file for 2025/26. Other income, gains, charges or an HMRC notice can still create a requirement. Use the current HMRC checker and obtain confirmation before ignoring a notice to file.

Use the current HMRC check

Do not rely on an old article that says everyone above a particular employment-income figure must file. HMRC’s current checker considers the tax year and reasons a return may be needed. If HMRC has issued a notice to file, address it rather than ignoring it because of a general rule you read online.

Review income beyond the payslip

Tell the accountant about rental income, self-employment, savings, dividends and disposals. Pension contributions, benefits and other circumstances may also need review. An employer deducting PAYE does not mean every part of your wider position has been dealt with.

Separate a filing requirement from an advice need

Someone may want help checking a tax position without necessarily needing a full annual return. Equally, a return may still be needed for a reason unrelated to salary. Ask what service is appropriate before paying.

Avoid assuming that every high earner is eligible for a refund or that a pension payment will automatically solve the issue.

Example: salary plus another income source

Two people with the same employment salary may have different filing requirements if one also has rental income, dividends or taxable disposals. The salary figure alone cannot establish that their tax administration is identical.

Should I ignore a notice to file if I think no return is needed?

No. Contact HMRC or ask the accountant to deal with the notice appropriately. Reading a general exception is not the same as having an issued filing requirement withdrawn.

Can I still ask for a review without a mandatory return?

Yes, subject to the provider offering and agreeing that work. Be clear whether you need a filing service, a check of a particular issue or broader advice. Avoid paying for a return purely because an outdated threshold article told you every high earner must file.

Next step: Check HMRC’s current tool and explain your complete circumstances to TaxSimba so the required work can be confirmed.

What to do if salary is your only income

For 2025/26, do not use an old “salary over £100,000” or “over £150,000” rule as a blanket filing instruction. Run HMRC’s current checker with your actual facts. If HMRC has already issued a notice to file and the check suggests no return is needed, ask it to confirm withdrawal rather than ignoring the notice.

Separately check rental income, self-employment, investments, gains and any charge not collected through PAYE. A return can still be needed for another reason even where salary alone would not require one.

Check the reason for filing beyond salary

Illustrative preparation example.

Your employment income is fully under PAYE, but you also have savings, dividends or a notice to file. Use the current checker with the whole picture. Do not decide the filing position from salary alone or from an old salary threshold in another guide.

Check: What other income, charge or HMRC notice affects the reporting requirement?

Actions to take
CheckPractical action

Is there income beyond PAYE?List trading, property, savings, dividends and relevant disposals.
Has HMRC issued a notice to file?Address the notice and seek withdrawal where appropriate instead of simply ignoring it.

Does PAYE prove all my tax is settled?

No. PAYE deductions may not cover separate income, benefits or every adjustment in your wider position.

Should I buy a return service solely because my salary is high?

title: Lost Receipts Before Your Tax Return? What to Do Next
excerpt: Missing receipts do not justify inventing expenses or ignoring the tax return. Start rebuilding the evidence and tell your accountant what is missing as early as possible.
metaTitle: Lost Receipts Before Self Assessment: Rebuild Evidence | TaxSimba
metaDescription: Missing tax records? Request duplicates, reconstruct transactions and distinguish estimated from provisional figures before approving your return.
featuredImageAlt: A trader reconstructs a missing receipt using bank evidence, supplier email and diary notes; no fake documents.

sources.label: GOV.UK — Business records if you're self-employed: How long to keep your records

content:
Rebuild the evidence from suppliers, bank records and other reliable documents, and tell the accountant what is missing. Do not invent costs. If figures remain uncertain near the deadline, check HMRC’s rules for estimates or provisional figures and correct them when the evidence arrives.

Try to replace the records

Ask suppliers for duplicate invoices, download bank statements and search email accounts or booking systems. Keep the reconstructed evidence in one place. A bank payment can help identify a transaction, but may not explain exactly what was bought or whether it was for business.

Mark what is uncertain

Prepare a list of missing items with the date, amount and explanation. Distinguish a figure you expect to confirm later from one that cannot be fully verified. Your accountant needs that distinction to consider how the return should describe the figures.

HMRC has guidance for estimated and provisional figures where records cannot be replaced. The return may need an explanation, and provisional figures need updating when actual figures become available.

Do not hide the problem until approval

The accountant should know the evidence limits before presenting the return for your review. Ask what can be supported, what needs more work and whether anything should be excluded.

Improve the routine afterwards

Capture documents regularly and check that uploads are readable. A photo of a receipt is only useful if it shows the relevant details.

Example: a supplier invoice is missing

A bank payment and order email can help identify the transaction. Ask the supplier for a duplicate and give the accountant the evidence available. Do not create a substitute receipt that pretends to be the original.

Is a round-number estimate acceptable by default?

No. Try to reconstruct actual figures first. If that cannot be done, tell the accountant why and keep the working behind any estimate. The appropriate disclosure and treatment depend on the circumstances.

What if I later find the document?

Tell the accountant whether the return has been submitted and how the confirmed amount compares with the figure used. A provisional amount is not meant to remain untouched once the actual information becomes available.

Next step: Send TaxSimba the records you have and a clear missing-record list, so the accountant can assess the next steps without guessing.

Create a replacement-evidence log

Illustrative preparation example.

For a lost receipt, record the supplier, date, amount, purpose and evidence requested. Attach a duplicate invoice or other reliable support if obtained. Mark unresolved items openly for the accountant rather than inserting a round-number expense with no explanation.

Check: Which amount is evidenced and which remains an estimate needing review?

Actions to take
CheckPractical action
Can the original evidence be replaced?Request supplier copies and recover bank, email or platform records first.
What exactly remains uncertain?List the date, amount, purpose and evidence gap for each item.
Is the figure estimated or awaiting confirmation?Agree the appropriate disclosure and follow-up rather than leaving a provisional figure indefinitely.

Does a bank payment guarantee an expense claim?

No. It may not establish the item, business purpose or private-use split. Provide all available supporting context.

What if I find the receipt after filing?

Compare it with the amount used and tell the accountant. A correction or update may be needed depending on the difference and how the return was completed.

  • Request supplier or platform duplicates.
  • Recover bank and email evidence.
  • Document the basis of any unavoidable estimate.
  • Track provisional figures until actual amounts are known.

title: Child Benefit and Self Assessment: Check Whether PAYE Is an Option
excerpt: A High Income Child Benefit Charge does not always mean you need Self Assessment solely for that charge. HMRC now provides a PAYE route where the qualifying conditions are met.
metaTitle: Child Benefit Charge: PAYE or Self Assessment? | TaxSimba
metaDescription: Check whether the High Income Child Benefit Charge can be paid through PAYE, confirm the tax year and consider other reasons you may still need a return.
featuredImageAlt: A parent checks Child Benefit letters and PAYE records with an adviser, family photo and careful paperwork.

sources.label: GOV.UK — High Income Child Benefit Charge: Pay the tax charge through PAYE
GOV.UK — Personal Allowances: adjusted net income
GOV.UK — Check if you need to send a Self Assessment tax return

content:
You may be able to pay the High Income Child Benefit Charge through PAYE instead of filing solely for that charge. Check the current conditions and whether any other reason still requires Self Assessment. Do not stop filing an issued return without resolving the notice.

Check the conditions before paying for a return

The PAYE option can apply when you do not need a return for another reason, are paying for the relevant current or previous year and act within HMRC’s permitted timeframe. For 2025/26, the guidance gives 31 January 2027 as the relevant cut-off for this option.

If you have self-employment or another reason to file, the position can be different. Use HMRC’s current guidance rather than assuming the charge is the only issue.

Bring the household facts

Tell the accountant who received Child Benefit, the relevant dates and the income information needed to assess the charge. Adjusted net income is not always the same as salary or the amount paid into your bank.

Do not simply stop filing

If you have previously filed only because of the charge, HMRC explains how to contact it about leaving Self Assessment and registering for PAYE collection instead. Do not ignore an outstanding notice to file.

A useful distinction

Child Benefit received, the person responsible for any charge and the method of paying that charge are separate questions. Give the accountant the household and income facts rather than assuming the recipient alone must always file.

Does PAYE collection deal with my other income?

Not automatically. A PAYE route for this charge does not settle separate self-employment, rental or other reporting requirements. Check the complete position before deciding that no return is needed.

What if I have already received a filing notice?

Address it with HMRC. Do not stop filing without checking the steps needed to leave Self Assessment where appropriate. Keep confirmation of the arrangement and review it if circumstances change. The availability of a route can also depend on the year and timing.

Next step: Check the current HMRC conditions first. If you need a return for other income or want the wider position reviewed, explain that to TaxSimba before choosing a package.

Review both partners’ relevant income

Illustrative preparation example.

Gather the Child Benefit figures and relevant income information before deciding who has a charge and how it is reported. Keep pension and donation evidence available where they affect adjusted net income. A PAYE route for the charge does not resolve an unrelated notice to file.

Check: Has the whole reporting position been checked before deciding to leave Self Assessment?

Actions to take
CheckPractical action
Who is responsible for the charge?Check the relevant household facts and adjusted net income, not only who receives the payments.
Does the PAYE route fit the year and timing?Use HMRC's current conditions before choosing collection through a tax code.
Is a return required for another reason?Review all income and deal with any existing filing notice.

Does the benefit recipient always pay the charge?

Not necessarily. Responsibility depends on the applicable household and income rules. Supply both partners' relevant details.

Can I stop filing once I request PAYE collection?

Do not assume so. Follow HMRC's process for any existing return requirement and retain confirmation.

  • Gather both partners' relevant income information.

  • Check PAYE-route timing and eligibility.
  • Resolve other filing reasons and existing notices.

title: Pension Contributions and Adjusted Net Income: What to Tell Your Accountant
excerpt: Pension contributions can affect a tax calculation, but the accountant needs to know how the contributions were made. A total described simply as “my pension payments” may not be enough.
metaTitle: Pensions and Adjusted Net Income: Avoid Double Relief | TaxSimba
metaDescription: Prepare pension contribution records by tax year and method, distinguish relief at source from payroll treatment and avoid claiming the same relief twice.
featuredImageAlt: A professional brings pension contribution evidence and payslips to an accountant, retirement planning scrapbook.

sources.label: GOV.UK — Claim tax relief on your private pension payments
GOV.UK — Personal Allowances: adjusted net income
GOV.UK — Private pension tax relief

content:
Tell the accountant whether contributions used relief at source, net pay or salary sacrifice. The tax and adjusted-net-income treatment differs. Do not subtract a contribution twice or assume a payment made after the tax-year end can simply be backdated.

Identify the contribution method

Gather pension statements and relevant payslips. Explain whether contributions came from pay, were paid personally or involved salary sacrifice. Different tax-relief methods mean the same-looking payment should not automatically be entered in the same place.

HMRC’s guidance explains the treatment of relief-at-source contributions and claims for additional relief. Avoid claiming relief twice where it has already been given through another mechanism.

Explain the wider income picture

Adjusted net income can matter for the Personal Allowance and other income-related rules. The accountant needs the relevant income and contribution details, not only your headline salary.

Timing is important. Identify the date contributions were paid and the tax year concerned. Do not assume a payment made now can retrospectively fix the previous year’s position.

Get advice before making a large payment

Tax treatment, contribution limits and the suitability of a pension decision need their own review. A tax-return article is not a recommendation to invest or transfer money.

Example: a personal contribution statement

If you made a payment personally, provide the statement showing the contribution and any tax relief added by the provider. Do not enter the same contribution again as though it were a separate payroll deduction.

Can I claim additional relief automatically?

The answer depends on the contribution method, income and relevant limits. Basic-rate relief already added by a provider does not settle every higher-rate claim, but it must be accounted for to avoid duplication.

Can I backdate a contribution by changing the description?

No. Give the accountant the actual payment dates. Ask about the rules before making decisions; allowances or carry-forward concepts do not mean a new payment can simply be described as paid in an earlier tax year.

Next step: Send TaxSimba the pension documents and explain what you want checked. The accountant can review the tax-return treatment within the agreed scope and identify where separate specialist advice is needed.

What grossing up looks like

Illustration: an £800 personal contribution under relief at source normally becomes £1,000 after the provider adds £200 basic-rate relief. Give the accountant both figures and the scheme method. Do not treat £1,000 as the cash payment and gross it up again. Net-pay contributions and salary sacrifice work differently; do not apply this example to them.

Identify the pension method from the evidence

Illustrative preparation example.

A payslip and a private pension statement describe contributions differently. Label which amounts are relief at source, net pay or salary sacrifice before supplying a total. Adding every displayed figure can deduct the same contribution twice.

Check: What method applies to each payment, and which figure belongs in the tax calculation?

Actions to take
CheckPractical action
How was the contribution made?Identify relief at source, net pay, salary sacrifice or another arrangement.
Which tax year received the payment?Use actual payment dates and provider evidence.
Has relief already been given elsewhere?Reconcile payroll and provider records before entering a claim.

Can a payment made now be backdated to last year?

Do not relabel the date. Carry-forward concepts do not make a new contribution a payment in an earlier tax year.

Does basic-rate relief mean no further action is ever needed?

Not necessarily. Additional relief can depend on the method and tax position. Have the evidence checked without duplicating relief already given.

Download a checklist for this guide

  • Collect provider statements and payslips.
  • Identify the contribution and relief method.
  • Record net, relief and gross amounts correctly.
  • Allocate payments to the actual tax year.
  • Flag limits or large contributions for a separate review.

title: Crypto Swaps and Tax: Why Not Cashing Out Does Not Settle the Question
excerpt: Keeping money inside a crypto exchange does not automatically mean there is no tax event. Exchanging one token for another can require a Capital Gains Tax calculation even when no pounds reach your bank.
metaTitle: Crypto Swaps and Tax: No Cash Withdrawal Needed | TaxSimba
metaDescription: Crypto-to-crypto exchanges can be disposals. Prepare exchange and wallet histories, distinguish own-wallet transfers and check income events separately.
featuredImageAlt: A crypto user records an exchange between two abstract token symbols on laptop and preserves transaction history, no coin logos.

sources.label: GOV.UK — Check if you need to pay tax when you sell cryptoassets
GOV.UK — CRYPTO10400 - Introduction to cryptoassets: record keeping - HMRC internal manual

content:
A token-to-token exchange can be a taxable disposal even if no pounds leave the exchange. Keep the GBP value, acquisition history, fees and transaction records. Income received in crypto can raise a separate question from any later gain or loss on disposal.

Reconstruct the transactions, not just the balance

Keep exports from every exchange and wallet involved. Record transfers clearly so moving assets between your own wallets is not confused with a sale. The accountant needs dates, quantities, values and relevant costs to understand the sequence.

HMRC identifies sales, exchanges and certain other disposals as events that may give rise to a gain. A later fall in the portfolio value does not, by itself, explain the tax treatment of an earlier disposal.

Separate income events from later disposals

Tokens received through certain activities can raise different tax questions from tokens simply bought and held. Tell the accountant about staking, rewards or payments received rather than including only trades against pounds.

Check the specialist work before purchasing

Large transaction histories, missing records and complex products can require additional calculations. Do not assume a standard SA package includes unlimited crypto reconciliation or every specialist issue.

Export records while access is available. An exchange balance today is not a substitute for the historical evidence needed for the return.

Example: a token-to-token exchange

A person exchanges one cryptoasset for another and keeps everything on the platform. No pounds are withdrawn, but the exchange can still be a disposal needing calculation. Later movements in the new asset’s value are a separate part of the history.

Is the platform’s profit figure enough?

Not always. Transfers, holdings on other exchanges and earlier acquisition records can affect the calculation. Keep exports and explain gaps rather than assuming one dashboard captures the whole history.

Does a loss mean there is nothing to report?

Do not decide solely from the current portfolio balance. Ask the accountant about realised transactions and any relevant reporting or loss claims. Confirm specialist support and the fee before commissioning a large reconciliation; a standard annual-return package should not be assumed to cover every crypto product.

Next step: Ask TaxSimba to confirm whether the crypto work can be supported, what records are required and the agreed fee before proceeding.

No cash withdrawal, but still a disposal

Imagine a token acquired for £400 is exchanged for another token when the amount disposed of is worth £700. There is a disposal to assess even though no pounds reach the bank. £300 is only a simple before-fees difference: the actual gain needs the UK matching rules, acquisition history, fees and other relevant transactions. Keep GBP values at the transaction time.

Record the value of both sides of a swap

Illustrative preparation example.

Keep the time, tokens exchanged, GBP value, fees and acquisition history when swapping one token for another. A wallet showing no withdrawal to a bank does not remove the need to review disposals. Transfers between your own wallets need identifying separately.

Check: Can the transaction be traced without treating every wallet movement as a new purchase or sale?

Actions to take
CheckPractical action
What was sold, swapped or spent?Build a disposal history with dates, quantities, sterling values and relevant costs.
Which movements are your own-wallet transfers?Link the sending and receiving records to prevent duplicate or false disposals.
Were tokens received as income?Identify rewards, payments and other receipts separately for tax review.

Does keeping assets on an exchange prevent tax?

No. A disposal can occur without withdrawing pounds. The transaction type and facts matter.

Can one platform's profit figure cover everything?

Not necessarily. Holdings and transactions elsewhere, missing acquisition costs and UK matching rules can change the calculation.

Download a checklist for this guide

  • Export all exchange and wallet histories.
  • Identify acquisitions, swaps, sales and spending.
  • Link own-wallet transfers.
  • Record rewards and other income events separately.
  • Agree specialist calculation scope before commissioning work.

title: MTD Standard or Calendar Update Periods: Which Should You Use?
excerpt: MTD update dates should match the reporting basis selected for your business. Standard and calendar update periods have the same submission deadlines, but cover different dates. Check the setting before your first update is sent.
metaTitle: MTD Standard vs Calendar Periods: Check Before Filing | TaxSimba
metaDescription: Compare MTD standard and calendar update periods, cumulative dates and shared deadlines, and check the software setting before the first submission.
featuredImageAlt: A trader compares two calendars with different month boundaries while an accountant checks software period settings.

sources.label: GOV.UK — Use Making Tax Digital for Income Tax - Send quarterly updates - Guidance

content:
Standard and calendar MTD updates use different coverage dates but the same deadlines. Select calendar periods in the software before sending the first update if that is the correct basis. Once an update is sent, HMRC does not allow a change for the rest of that tax year.

The two reporting options

Standard periods follow the tax year. For 2026/27, the cumulative second update covers 6 April to 5 October 2026 and is due by 7 November 2026. Calendar periods suit an accounting period from 1 April to 31 March. The corresponding second update covers 1 April to 30 September 2026 and has the same deadline.

The later updates also build on the year so far. A third standard update covers 6 April 2026 to 5 January 2027; it is not just the transactions since October. The calendar equivalent runs from 1 April to 31 December 2026.

Can you switch after filing?

HMRC says to select calendar periods in compatible software before sending the first quarterly update. Once an update has been sent, you cannot change the periods for the rest of that tax year. If a previous accountant has already filed, check the existing setting before creating replacement records.

What to give your accountant

Provide your accounting year-end, the reporting basis already selected and copies of any earlier submission confirmations. A bank statement ending at month-end does not, by itself, establish which HMRC reporting periods you use.

For example, a landlord keeping monthly records may prefer calendar periods. That preference still needs to be reflected correctly in the software; it should not be assumed from how the landlord names folders.

Keep the dashboard and submission dates consistent

Your service dashboard may display separate work stages for each quarter. Those stages should not be confused with the cumulative totals sent to HMRC. Ask your accountant to confirm both the period being reviewed and the year-to-date coverage of the submission.

Before changing providers, tell TaxSimba whether any update has already been submitted. This helps the accountant continue the existing reporting basis without accidentally omitting or duplicating days.

Check the basis already used in software

Illustrative preparation example.

Before comparing an export with an update, recover the first submission and the selected standard or calendar basis. A period ending on 30 September is not interchangeable with one ending on 5 October. Keep the same basis visible throughout the year.

Check: Which reporting basis does the existing submission evidence show?

Actions to take
CheckPractical action
Which period option is actually selected?Check the software and earlier submissions rather than inferring it from file names.
Do records cover the cumulative window?Reconcile from the relevant start of year through the update end date.
Has the first update already been sent?Confirm the existing setting before making a provider or software change.

Are calendar periods just different submission deadlines?

No. They change the date coverage. The published submission deadlines are the same for the corresponding update.

Can a new accountant choose a different basis mid-year?

Not simply after an update has been sent. Supply the current setting and submission history so the year continues consistently.

title: MTD Records Below £90,000: When Simpler Categorisation Applies
excerpt: Some businesses can categorise MTD records in less detail. This can reduce the number of categories used, but it does not remove the need for digital records, accurate figures or quarterly updates.
metaTitle: MTD Simpler Categorisation: The £90,000 Test | TaxSimba
metaDescription: Check eligibility for simpler MTD categories, keep supporting records and identify restricted property finance costs and any turnover-triggered change.
featuredImageAlt: A smaller business owner compares detailed expense categories with a simpler income-and-expense summary ledger.

sources.label: GOV.UK — Use Making Tax Digital for Income Tax - Create digital records - Guidance

content:
HMRC permits simpler income-and-expense categorisation below the applicable £90,000 turnover limit, subject to its conditions. This does not remove digital records or updates. Check the business, year and treatment when turnover reaches the limit before using the simplified categories.

What the £90,000 figure means

HMRC permits simpler categorisation where turnover from a self-employment source, or total UK property turnover, is less than £90,000. The guidance applies the test to the relevant income source. Foreign property has its own treatment, so do not apply the UK turnover test automatically to overseas rent.

For an eligible sole trader, a transaction may be recorded as income or an expense without selecting a detailed expense category. A UK residential landlord must still identify restricted finance costs separately. Mortgage interest should therefore not disappear into a single general expenses total.

Simpler categories still need supporting records

Keep invoices, receipts, statements and explanations of business use. A simpler category is not permission to claim personal spending or to report only the money left in the bank. Your accountant still needs to establish the correct taxable result at year-end.

For example, a £70,000-turnover sole trader might qualify for less detailed categorisation. That does not establish whether the person must register for VAT, because VAT uses its own taxable-turnover rules and tests.

What if turnover reaches £90,000?

HMRC requires full categorisation for that income source, including records from the beginning of the current tax year and in the following tax year. Leaving the change until the next update can create extra bookkeeping work. If turnover is likely to reach the limit, detailed categories from the start may be more practical.

Agree a method before records are imported

Tell your accountant about every trade and property business, expected turnover and existing categories. Where you have several sources, check eligibility source by source against HMRC's current conditions.

TaxSimba's accountant can maintain the agreed records from the information you provide. Ask which recording approach fits your business rather than assuming that being below a threshold removes the underlying work.

Plan for the limit before simplifying categories

Illustrative preparation example.

If turnover is close to the applicable limit, keep enough detail to support fuller categories. A single total may save time today but create reconstruction work if eligibility changes. Check the relevant source and conditions rather than assuming all personal income shares one test.

Check: Could the records still support the required categories if the turnover limit is reached?

Actions to take
CheckPractical action
Which source and turnover test apply?Check each relevant trade or property business under current HMRC conditions.
Are restricted finance costs separate?Keep residential property finance costs identifiable even where simpler categories are available.
Is turnover approaching the limit?Plan for full categorisation and any required review from the year's start.

Does simpler categorisation mean fewer records?

No. The level of category detail may change, but complete income, costs and supporting evidence are still needed.

Is this the same as a VAT-registration test?

No. VAT has its own taxable-turnover rules. Do not use a simpler-record category decision to decide VAT registration.
