title: Self-Employed and a Landlord: How Your MTD Updates Fit Together
excerpt: If you run a sole trader business and receive rental income, the income may be combined when checking whether MTD applies. That does not mean all the bookkeeping belongs in one business update.
metaTitle: Sole Trader and Landlord: Separate MTD Updates | TaxSimba
metaDescription: Trade and rental income can combine for MTD eligibility while needing separate business records and updates. Plan the complete reporting workflow.
featuredImageAlt: A person with a trade and rental property maintains two separate update folders, tools and house model.

sources.label: GOV.UK — Use Making Tax Digital for Income Tax - Create digital records - Guidance
GOV.UK — Use Making Tax Digital for Income Tax - Send quarterly updates - Guidance

content:
Relevant trade and property income can be added together for MTD eligibility while still needing separate updates. Keep the income-source records distinct and avoid counting transfers as fresh income. The annual return then brings the person’s wider tax position together.

Separate the income sources

An existing sole trader business and an existing UK property business need their own digital records and quarterly updates where those sources fall within your MTD obligations. UK rental properties generally form one UK property business, rather than a separate reporting business for each address.

A foreign property business is separate again. Tell your accountant about it even if the money remains abroad. Residence, reliefs and software support need checking before the reporting route is agreed.

Why a shared bank account needs care

Imagine a self-employed consultant who also rents out a flat. A client invoice, tenant payment and personal transfer might all arrive in the same account. The accountant must identify which belongs to the trade, which belongs to the property business and which is not income at all.

A single bank feed cannot make those decisions reliably without supporting information. Supply invoices, rental statements, property costs and explanations for transfers so the separate records can be maintained correctly.

One annual personal tax position

The quarterly updates are summaries for the relevant businesses. Your annual Income Tax return brings the wider tax position together, including other reportable income, adjustments and reliefs. Sending a property update does not complete the trade update or the annual return.

Small sources, newly started businesses and particular reliefs can affect which records are required and when. Do not remove a source simply because its profit is low; explain the full position to your accountant.

Confirm scope at the start

Before buying support, identify how many trades you have, whether you receive UK or foreign rent, and what has already been submitted. Ask TaxSimba to confirm that the selected service covers those sources and any earlier work requiring attention. Clear scope helps prevent a second business being discovered only when a deadline approaches.

Keep the trade and property receipt trails distinct

Illustrative preparation example.

A customer pays the trade while a tenant pays rent into the same account. Identify both sources and any transfers before producing the required business summaries. Adding sources for eligibility does not mean combining unrelated totals into one quarterly update.

Check: Can each required business update be reconciled to its own records?

Can mixed transactions be explained?Use source records and clear tags for trade, rent and non-income transfers.

Does one property update complete my trade's reporting?

No. Each relevant business needs its own required reporting. Track submissions by source and period.

Do several UK flats mean several UK property businesses?

They generally form one UK property business. Keep property-level evidence while checking the correct reporting structure.

title: Main or Supporting MTD Accountant: Who Files Your Annual Return?
excerpt: MTD allows a main agent and supporting agents to help with different tasks. The distinction matters if one person keeps your books and another prepares your annual tax return. Agree who does what before authorising a new accountant.
metaTitle: Main vs Supporting MTD Agent: Who Files the Return? | TaxSimba
metaDescription: Check MTD agent roles, annual-return responsibility and record handovers before authorising an accountant or bookkeeper for quarterly work.
featuredImageAlt: A main accountant and supporting bookkeeper divide records, updates and annual-return work at one desk.

sources.label: GOV.UK — Choose agents for Making Tax Digital for Income Tax
GOV.UK — Use Making Tax Digital for Income Tax - Submit your tax return - Guidance

content:
A main MTD agent can handle the overall annual-return role; supporting agents have narrower permissions for the work they are authorised to do. Agree who keeps the books, sends updates and finalises the return. Authorising another firm is not a substitute for that handover agreement.

What a main agent does

A main agent can manage the overall MTD tax position and submit the annual return. HMRC allows only one main agent at a time. Replacing that authorisation can affect the accountant who was previously responsible, so tell both providers about a planned change.

What a supporting agent does

A supporting agent can help with tasks such as digital records and quarterly updates, but cannot submit the annual MTD Income Tax return as your main agent. There can be more than one supporting agent, and their access is more limited.

Having someone authorised for quarterly work therefore does not establish that the annual return is covered. Check the engagement, the HMRC authorisation and the practical handover arrangements together.

Avoid two people filing overlapping figures

If several people work on the same business, HMRC requires one combined update for each update period. A bookkeeper should not send one version while an accountant independently sends another incomplete version of the same business totals.

For example, you might maintain sales records while a supporting bookkeeper records expenses. Someone must reconcile the whole record before the agreed agent submits the update. Access to software is not a substitute for agreeing that responsibility.

Questions to settle in writing

Identify who maintains records, who sends updates, who deals with corrections, who gathers other personal income and who prepares the annual return. Confirm how records and submission evidence will pass between the people involved.

When joining TaxSimba, disclose any existing accountant or bookkeeper and their current role. TaxSimba can then confirm the authorisation and work required for your agreed service. You should retain your own Government Gateway credentials; authorised agent access should not depend on giving another person your password or security codes.

Name the person who closes the annual return

Illustrative preparation example.

A bookkeeper has supporting-agent access and an accountant handles the annual position. Record who supplies missing information and who obtains final approval. Keep that agreement beside the permissions so a completed update is not mistaken for annual-return responsibility.

Check: Who is the main agent responsible for the final return, and what remains with the supporting agent?

Not in the main-agent role required for that work. Confirm the appropriate authorisation and annual-return arrangement.

Does software access prove a task is included in the fee?

No. Check the engagement as well as technical permissions. An authorised person may still have a limited agreed scope.

title: Why Your MTD Tax Estimate May Differ From Your Final Bill
excerpt: The tax estimate displayed after an MTD update is a working estimate, not your final annual tax bill. Its usefulness depends on the records submitted and the other information HMRC has about you.
metaTitle: MTD Tax Estimates: Why the Final Bill Can Differ | TaxSimba
metaDescription: Understand the limits of an MTD tax estimate, identify missing income and adjustments, and distinguish estimated liability from the amount still payable.
featuredImageAlt: A trader compares a provisional tax estimate on screen with a fuller annual tax record, extra income papers arriving.

sources.label: GOV.UK — Use Making Tax Digital for Income Tax - Send quarterly updates - Guidance

content:
An MTD estimate is not necessarily your final liability or the balance left to pay. Missing income, reliefs, year-end adjustments and tax already deducted can change those figures. Use it for planning, then check the final calculation and HMRC account.

What the estimate can include

HMRC uses the self-employment and property figures reported so far, together with other information it already holds. Depending on your software, additional income may also be supplied during the year. Information that has not yet been reported can leave the estimate incomplete.

For example, a landlord may also have employment income, savings interest and dividends. A property update alone does not tell the whole story. If part of that wider income is missing, the estimate may not reflect the tax band that eventually applies.

Year-end adjustments can change the result

Quarterly updates summarise records; they do not require all the accounting and tax adjustments needed for the annual return. Business-use adjustments, reliefs and other year-end calculations can change the final liability. An accounting year that differs from the tax year may also make an interim estimate less straightforward.

Avoid taking money out of your tax savings account solely because a screen shows a lower figure than expected. Ask your accountant which assumptions sit behind it and whether anything important is missing.

Tax liability and amount still to pay differ

An estimated liability is not necessarily the outstanding balance after payments, credits or payments on account. Check which figure you are looking at. The annual calculation and HMRC account need to be reconciled before deciding what remains payable.

Make the estimate more useful

Keep business records current and tell your accountant about other income, changes in employment, pensions, student loans and significant one-off transactions. Explain unusual entries rather than allowing an incorrect category to carry forward.

TaxSimba's accountant can review the figures available within the agreed service and explain what further information is needed. Use the estimate to support sensible planning, while keeping the final return, the payment position and the service subscription fee clearly separate.

Explain the difference between three tax figures

Illustrative preparation example.

Your software shows an in-year estimate, the draft annual calculation shows another amount and the HMRC account shows a balance after payments. Compare their dates and what they include. They can describe different stages rather than a single unexplained software error.

Check: Which figure is an estimate, which is total liability and which is still payable?

Actions to take
CheckPractical action
What information underlies the estimate?Check reported business figures and any other income or reliefs already included.
Which year-end adjustments are outstanding?Identify business-use, accounting and tax adjustments before treating the figure as final.
Is the screen showing liability or balance due?Reconcile payments, credits and dated charges separately.

Can an estimate change even if quarterly records were accurate?

Yes. Other income, reliefs and year-end adjustments can affect the final result.

Does an estimated bill mean tax is payable every quarter?

No. Reporting and payment rules are separate. Check the actual HMRC statement and payment dates.

title: Does Partnership Income Put You Into MTD for Income Tax?
excerpt: An individual partner's share of partnership profit is not the same as income from a separate sole trader business. Do not assume that a large partnership allocation automatically brings that income into the current MTD quarterly reporting rules.
metaTitle: Partnership Income and MTD: Check Separate Sources | TaxSimba
metaDescription: Distinguish partnership profit from sole-trader and property income for MTD, and gather the partnership statement for your complete personal return.
featuredImageAlt: Business partners review a partnership agreement while one partner keeps a separate sole-trade ledger.

sources.label: GOV.UK — Find out if and when you need to use Making Tax Digital for Income Tax
GOV.UK — Use Making Tax Digital for Income Tax - Create digital records - Guidance

content:
An individual’s share of partnership profits is generally outside the current MTD qualifying-income test. A separate personal trade or property business can still bring the individual into MTD. Do not confuse the partnership’s turnover with personal sole-trader income.

Separate the partnership from your other work

HMRC's current MTD guidance treats partnership profit differently from sole trader and property income. Your share of partnership profit does not itself require the same MTD digital records as an individual sole trader business. A partnership's own return is also a separate obligation from your personal return.

If you have a sole trader business or property income as well, those sources can still bring you into MTD. Check the relevant qualifying income and start-year rules for those activities rather than treating all income on your return as one turnover figure.

An example of mixed income

Suppose you receive an allocation of partnership profit and also rent out a personally owned flat. The partnership allocation and the rental business need to be identified separately. The rental income may affect MTD eligibility even though partnership profit does not follow the same quarterly-record rules.

The annual personal return must still include all reportable income. Income being outside the quarterly records does not make it exempt from Income Tax.

Collect the partnership information early

Ask for the partnership's tax reference, your partnership statement, the period covered and details of tax already deducted or reliefs relevant to your share. Do not substitute drawings from the partnership bank account for the taxable profit allocated to you.

Check future rules without assuming a start date

MTD expansion announcements should be distinguished from the rules currently applying to your circumstances. A threshold change for sole traders and landlords does not, by itself, establish a partnership reporting start date.

Before appointing TaxSimba, explain any partnership involvement so the accountant can confirm whether your personal return and other income are within the proposed scope. Preparation of the partnership's own accounts or return should be agreed separately if required; it should not be assumed from a personal tax package.

Do not use partnership turnover as personal turnover

Illustrative preparation example.

Keep the partnership statement separate from any personal sole trade and rental records. The partnership’s gross receipts are not automatically the individual partner’s personal trading receipts for MTD entry. The wider annual return still needs the relevant partnership information.

Check: Which activity is a partnership and which is a separate personal business?

title: MTD and Limited Company Directors: Which Income Counts?
excerpt: Being a limited company director does not automatically mean your company's turnover belongs in your personal MTD for Income Tax calculation. The company and you are separate taxpayers, with different reporting responsibilities.
metaTitle: MTD and Company Directors: Which Income Counts? | TaxSimba
metaDescription: Separate company turnover, salary and dividends from personal trading and property income before checking a director's MTD obligations.
featuredImageAlt: A limited-company director keeps company turnover separate from personal dividends, salary and a private rental folder.

sources.label: GOV.UK — Find out if and when you need to use Making Tax Digital for Income Tax

content:
A company’s turnover is not its director’s personal sole-trade income. Salary and dividends do not count towards MTD qualifying income in the same way as personal trade and property receipts. Check any separate self-employment or rental activity and keep the company filings distinct.

Start with the type of income

A director might receive a salary and dividends from a company, while also running a separate sole trader activity or receiving personally owned rental income. Those categories must be distinguished before MTD eligibility can be assessed.

Salary and dividends are not sole trader turnover. A company's sales are not automatically the director's personal business income either. Personally earned self-employment and property income are the sources to examine under the current MTD qualifying-income rules.

What if you own a rental property?

Company ownership and personal ownership produce different tax reporting. If you personally rent out a flat, its rental income may be relevant to your MTD position. If the company owns the property, do not place the company's rent into your personal MTD records merely because you control the company.

Provide the accountant with ownership documents and a clear explanation of which bank accounts receive the income. Where ownership or beneficial entitlement is uncertain, clarify it before preparing figures.

Personal and company returns remain separate

Your personal return may need salary, dividends, benefits and other income. The company can separately require accounts, a Corporation Tax return, payroll or other filings. Buying a personal Self Assessment or MTD service does not automatically purchase those company services.

A director who also has an MTD sole trader business must still ensure the annual personal return includes the wider reportable income. Quarterly business summaries do not replace that review.

Tell your accountant about every role

Supply your P60 or employment figures, dividend vouchers, relevant benefit information and details of personal trades or property. Separate company transactions from personal expenses and explain any director's loan account issues.

TaxSimba can confirm the scope of the personal tax service after reviewing those facts. Ask for company work to be identified and priced separately where needed, so the responsibilities are clear before any filing deadline.

Keep company receipts out of a personal trade

Illustrative preparation example.

A company receives sales revenue and pays its director salary or dividends. Do not relabel the company’s sales as the director’s personal sole-trade turnover. Check any separately owned rental property or genuine personal trade on its own facts.

Check: Which taxpayer earned each amount: the company or the individual?

Actions to take
CheckPractical action
Who legally owns the income source?Separate personally held businesses or property from company-owned activity.
What type of personal income is received?Distinguish salary, dividends, benefits, sole-trader receipts and personal rent.
Which services are included?Confirm company accounts, payroll and loan work separately from personal SA or MTD support.

Not simply because you own the company. Establish ownership and the correct taxpayer before recording the source.

Can a director also need MTD for a personal trade?

Yes. A separate personal trade or property source can bring its own obligations. Check the relevant gross income and start rules.

title: Starting a New Business or Rental Income While Already in MTD
excerpt: Starting another activity while you already use MTD does not always mean that its quarterly reporting starts immediately. First establish whether it is a genuinely new income source or an addition to an existing business.
metaTitle: New Business or Rent While in MTD: Check Start Dates | TaxSimba
metaDescription: Adding a trade or rental source while in MTD? Distinguish a new source from another UK property and check when digital records and updates become required.
featuredImageAlt: A trader adds a new rental-property folder to an existing digital-records system, keys and fresh planner.

sources.label: GOV.UK — Use Making Tax Digital for Income Tax - Add or cease income sources - Guidance
GOV.UK — New income sources and digital records

content:
If you are already in MTD and start a new trade or property source, keep its start date and transactions identifiable. HMRC has specific rules for when digital records and updates become compulsory for that new source; they do not necessarily start immediately. Check the first-return timing before setting its reporting schedule.

Another UK rental property is usually different

HMRC treats UK properties as one UK property business. If you already report that business through MTD and start receiving rent from another UK property, the new property's income and expenses join the existing business records from the relevant start point.

That is different from starting your first property business alongside an existing sole trade. It is also different from beginning a genuinely separate trade. Tell your accountant what changed rather than creating a second reporting source automatically.

A genuinely new income source has specific timing

HMRC's current guidance says a new self-employment or property source normally begins compulsory digital records and quarterly updates after it has first been included in an annual return. The source must still be reported on the correct annual return before that quarterly obligation begins.

In HMRC's example, a new source starting on 1 July 2026 is first included in the 2026/27 return, due by 31 January 2028. Digital records and quarterly updates for that source then start from 6 April 2028. HMRC also allows a choice to start reporting it earlier through the appropriate account setting.

Keep ordinary records from the beginning

This timing rule does not make early income tax-free or remove normal record-keeping duties. Keep receipts, income records and the actual start date from the outset. Otherwise the first annual return will be difficult to prepare accurately.

Check the software and service scope

The new source needs to be added to the appropriate HMRC account and supported by the filing software. Ask your accountant which start date and reporting option apply before expecting it to appear in an existing dashboard.

Tell TaxSimba before adding a new activity or property business. The accountant can distinguish the reporting obligation from the work needed to maintain your records and confirm any change to the agreed service.

Start a new-source file without assuming an immediate update

Illustrative preparation example.

Record the new source’s actual start date and keep its transactions identifiable. If you are already in MTD, check HMRC’s rules for when digital-record and quarterly duties start for that new source. An existing subscription alone does not answer that timing question.

Check: When is the new source first included in a return, and when do its MTD record duties start?

CheckPractical action

What start timing does HMRC require?Check the new-source rules and any permitted earlier reporting choice.
Are ordinary records already being kept?Capture receipts and costs from the start even before quarterly reporting becomes compulsory.

Does a new UK flat always need a new property-business update?

No. It generally joins an existing UK property business. Check any different ownership or overseas facts.

Is new-source income tax-free before its first quarterly update?

No. It still belongs on the correct annual return. Quarterly reporting timing does not remove the underlying tax duties.

title: Letting Agent Statements and MTD: Record Gross Rent, Not Just the Payout
excerpt: The payment a letting agent sends to your bank may already have fees and property costs deducted. Recording only that payment can understate both rental income and expenses, making the bookkeeping difficult to reconcile.
metaTitle: Letting Agent Statements: Gross Rent vs Net Payout | TaxSimba
metaDescription: Reconcile agent-collected rent, fees, repairs and bank payouts for MTD, identify unusual deductions and avoid counting the same rent twice.
featuredImageAlt: A landlord reconciles gross rent, letting-agent fees and net deposit using a letting statement and calculator.

sources.label: GOV.UK — Use Making Tax Digital for Income Tax - Create digital records - Guidance
GOV.UK — Work out your rental income when you let property

content:
Record the gross rent and identify the agent’s fees and other deductions separately. The amount deposited in your bank is often net of those charges. Reconcile the statement so neither the rent nor the same expense is counted twice.

Read the statement behind the deposit

Ask the agent for a statement showing rent collected, management fees, repairs paid on your behalf and the amount transferred to you. HMRC's digital-record guidance says that where you know only net income, obtain the full income figure and create records for the income and expenses.

For example, assume an agent collects £1,600 rent, deducts a £160 management charge and transfers £1,440. Recording only £1,440 as rent hides the gross income and the separate cost. Record the underlying amounts, then check whether the expense qualifies for tax relief.

Not every deduction has the same tax treatment

A management fee, a repair, an improvement and a residential mortgage finance cost can require different treatment. The fact that the agent has deducted an amount does not prove that it is an allowable expense against rental profit.

Security deposits and money held for future costs also need explanation. Do not treat every item on the agent's statement as current rental income or a deductible charge without checking what it represents.

Prevent the same rent being counted twice

Where the bank feed already contains the net transfer, the accountant should reconcile it to the statement. Adding gross rent as a separate sale without dealing with the transfer can duplicate income. The record should show how the collected rent, deductions and payout connect.

Keep each statement with the relevant property and period. If an agent pays late or a statement spans a year-end, your accounting method also affects the correct reporting treatment.

Give your accountant the full picture

Provide all agent statements, supporting invoices for unusual costs, details of ownership shares and any direct payments from tenants. TaxSimba can maintain the agreed rental records from that evidence. Sending only the bank deposit is rarely enough to explain the underlying rental activity clearly.

Check the statement against the deposit

Illustration: £1,200 gross rent less a £120 management fee leaves £1,080 paid to the bank. Keep the rent and fee separate instead of entering £1,080 as rent and deducting £120 again. A repair, deposit transfer or tax withheld can introduce other lines; retain the full statement and underlying documents.

Reconcile the agent’s deductions explicitly

Illustrative preparation example.

An agent receives £1,200 rent, keeps £120 in fees and pays £1,080 to you. The statement explains gross income of £1,200 and a separate £120 fee. Recording £1,080 rent and deducting £120 again counts the charge twice.

Check: Does the gross rent less each identified deduction equal the payout?

Actions to take
CheckPractical action
What rent was collected before deductions?Obtain the full statement and include direct tenant receipts separately.
What does each deduction represent?Distinguish fees, repairs, capital work, retained money and deposits.
Does the bank payout reconcile?Bridge gross rent to the transfer without counting both as separate income.

Is every amount withheld by an agent deductible?

No. Its nature and tax treatment still need checking. Keep invoices and explanations for unusual items.

What if an agent statement crosses the tax-year end?

Flag its coverage and payment dates. The accounting basis affects how amounts belong in the year.

title: Should You Join MTD Voluntarily Before Your Compulsory Start Date?
excerpt: You may be able to join MTD voluntarily before it becomes compulsory for you. Starting early can give you time to establish a recording routine, but it also brings work forward. Check the full reporting commitment before signing up.
metaTitle: Join MTD Voluntarily? Check the Full Commitment | TaxSimba
metaDescription: Considering early MTD signup? Check eligibility, the chosen tax year, software readiness and any catch-up records before committing to quarterly reporting.
featuredImageAlt: A small landlord discusses voluntary digital-records adoption with an adviser, readiness checklist and laptop.

sources.label: GOV.UK — Sign up for Making Tax Digital for Income Tax
GOV.UK — Use Making Tax Digital for Income Tax - Using Making Tax Digital for Income Tax for the first time  - Guidance

content:
You may be eligible to join MTD voluntarily before your compulsory date. Consider the record-keeping, software and reporting commitment as well as any benefit of starting early. Check your actual eligibility and future obligations before treating it as a trial with no consequences.

Confirm whether you are really volunteering

First check the income year and threshold that apply to you. A person already required to use MTD is not a volunteer simply because their accountant has not yet connected software. HMRC may also have signed up people within the compulsory 2026/27 population.

If your compulsory start is later, check whether HMRC allows you to volunteer for the current or following tax year and whether your circumstances and software are supported.

What starting early involves

You need compatible software, the required digital records, quarterly updates and an annual return through the MTD route. Joining partway through a tax year can mean catching up records and updates for the earlier part of that year.

For example, volunteering in autumn is not necessarily a promise to report only the remaining months. Establish the tax year selected and the records needed from its beginning before authorising the change.

Weigh the practical benefits

Early participation can help you test how records reach your accountant, how missing information is requested and how you review figures. It is most useful when the business information is available and both you and your accountant can support the reporting process.

It may be less suitable when an unresolved ownership question, incomplete records or unsupported income source still needs attention. Preparing for MTD does not always require joining immediately.

Understand penalties and other obligations

HMRC provides particular late-quarterly-update treatment for volunteers, but that should not be read as permission to ignore annual returns or payment obligations. Check the current rules for the year concerned.

Ask TaxSimba to confirm your proposed start year, available service and any catch-up work before purchase. A clear start plan is more useful than volunteering solely because an advert suggests that every taxpayer needs to join at once.

Decide whether early entry fits your records

Illustrative preparation example.

Before volunteering, test one month of complete records and agree who will maintain them. Check software support, applicable filing duties and the route if circumstances later change. Treat the choice as a reporting commitment rather than a demonstration account.

Check: What practical benefit justifies starting early, and who will complete the work?

Actions to take
CheckPractical action
Are you actually outside compulsory MTD today?Check the relevant year and threshold first.
What tax year are you joining for?Identify records and earlier updates needed for that selected year.
Can your software and adviser support the whole process?Confirm sources, authorisation, annual-return work and any catch-up fee.

Must I volunteer to practise better digital records?

No. You can improve records and prepare a workflow before deciding whether early signup is appropriate.

Does voluntary participation remove annual-return duties?

No. Check the current volunteer penalty treatment, but keep annual filing and payment obligations clear.

title: MTD From April 2028: What the £20,000 Threshold Means
excerpt: The MTD qualifying-income threshold is scheduled to fall again for April 2028. If your relevant income is above £20,000, that later start date may affect your planning. It does not mean everyone earning £20,000 must use MTD today.
metaTitle: MTD £20,000 Threshold: Planning for April 2028 | TaxSimba
metaDescription: Check the scheduled April 2028 MTD £20,000 threshold against 2026/27 gross qualifying income and distinguish later preparation from an existing obligation.
featuredImageAlt: A smaller trader plans future record-keeping with a long-term calendar and labelled-by-colour yearly folders.

sources.label: GOV.UK — Find out if and when you need to use Making Tax Digital for Income Tax

content:
The April 2028 phase is based on relevant qualifying income over £20,000 for 2026/27. It does not mean every person earning £20,000 must use MTD today. Use gross trade and property income and recheck the applicable HMRC rules before the start date.

Match the threshold to the income year

HMRC's current timetable brings in people with qualifying income over £50,000 for April 2026, over £30,000 for April 2027 and over £20,000 for April 2028. The corresponding tax returns and income years matter when establishing an individual's start date.

For the April 2028 stage, check qualifying income for 2026/27. Qualifying income concerns gross self-employment and property income, rather than the profit left after expenses. Salary is not simply added to that turnover figure.

Do not confuse turnover and take-home pay

A sole trader with substantial expenses might have profit below £20,000 while gross business income exceeds it. A landlord can similarly have rent above the threshold even after finance costs and other spending leave a much smaller cash surplus.

Give your accountant the gross figures for each relevant source and explain any jointly owned property, ceased activity or newly started business. Those details can affect the assessment.

What you can do before the start date

Keep business records consistently and retain statements from platforms or letting agents. Establish who will maintain digital records, which software will be used and who will send updates and prepare the annual return.

You do not have to treat every later-cohort enquiry as an immediate subscription purchase. Confirm the actual start year and decide whether earlier preparation or voluntary participation would be useful.

Recheck before acting

This article reflects the timetable checked on 20 October 2026. Future legislation, guidance or your circumstances can change, so review the position before the relevant tax year begins.

TaxSimba can discuss accountant-led support for the service period you need. Start with the eligibility question, then agree a suitable start date and scope rather than assuming that the date of an online enquiry is the date quarterly obligations begin.

Put April 2028 preparation against the right year

Illustrative preparation example.

Keep a 2026/27 schedule of relevant gross trade and property income for the April 2028 phase. Record the expected start separately from your current obligations. A future threshold should not be used to infer that an identical duty already applies today.

Check: Which year’s income supports the future start-date check?

Actions to take
CheckPractical action
Which income year supports the 2028 start?Check 2026/27 qualifying income under the published timetable.
Are the figures gross and complete?Combine relevant trading and property sources using the correct joint share.

title: Is a Receipt Photo Enough for MTD? What Your Records Need
excerpt: A photograph of a receipt can support an expense, but it is not automatically the complete digital transaction record required for MTD. The image and the accounting entry do different jobs.
metaTitle: Receipt Photos and MTD: Complete the Digital Record | TaxSimba
metaDescription: Receipt photos support MTD records but do not replace transaction entries. Check extracted dates, amounts, categories, business purpose and duplicate imports.
featuredImageAlt: A trader places a receipt photo beside a structured ledger entry, both evidence and record visibly distinct.

sources.label: GOV.UK — Use Making Tax Digital for Income Tax - Create digital records - Guidance
GOV.UK — Business records if you're self-employed: Overview

content:
A receipt photograph is supporting evidence, not automatically a complete MTD transaction record. The accounting entry still needs the relevant amount, date and category. Link the image to the entry and reconcile it to the payment without claiming it twice.

What the transaction record contains

HMRC's guidance requires digital information about the amount, date and appropriate category of income or expense. The detail depends on your business and whether a permitted simplification applies. The record must be created and stored using software within the MTD process.

A picture sitting in your phone gallery does not, by itself, establish that the expense has reached the accounting records. If receipt software extracts the details, someone still needs to check that the amount, date and category are correct.

Keep the reason for the spending

A receipt can show what was purchased without explaining why it was for the business. Add context for unusual items and identify personal use. Ordinary clothing or a private meal does not become deductible because it has been photographed.

For example, a receipt for a tool used partly at home may require a business-use adjustment. The image is useful evidence, while the accountant decides how the allowable amount should be reflected in the records.

Prevent duplicate expenses

The same cost might appear in a bank feed and in a receipt upload. Those should usually be matched rather than treated as two purchases. Tell your accountant if you submit the same document through more than one route or replace an unclear image.

Keep supporting documents legible, complete and accessible. Store them with enough detail to reconnect them to the accounting entry later; a cropped image without the date or supplier can be difficult to use.

Agree a simple handover routine

Ask how your accountant wants documents supplied and how they will tell you about missing information. Providing records regularly gives time to resolve questions before quarterly deadlines.

TaxSimba's accountant-led service uses the information you provide to maintain the agreed records. Uploading evidence starts that process; review, correct recording and the separate submission outcome still matter before an MTD update is treated as complete.

Test whether a photo became one correct record

Illustrative preparation example.

Open one receipt image and locate the resulting entry. Check that OCR has not read the date or amount incorrectly, and that a matching bank import did not create a duplicate. Keep the image as evidence linked to the agreed entry.

Check: Is there exactly one supported transaction for this receipt?

Were extracted details checked?Review amount, date, supplier, category and business purpose.
Does the same cost appear in a feed?Match the records and avoid duplicate expenses.

Does photographing a personal purchase make it deductible?

No. The business purpose and any private-use restriction still need checking.

Can I discard an unreadable original after uploading?

Ensure the retained evidence is complete and legible under the applicable record-keeping rules. Replace cropped or unclear images promptly.

title: MTD Software or HMRC Unavailable Near a Deadline: What to Do
excerpt: If MTD software stops working near a deadline, establish what failed and preserve the evidence. A failed login, missing authorisation and an HMRC service outage require different responses. None should be assumed from a general error message.
metaTitle: MTD Software or HMRC Outage: Evidence and Next Steps | TaxSimba
metaDescription: MTD unavailable near a deadline? Identify the failure, keep dated evidence, check official service notices and confirm the submission after recovery.
featuredImageAlt: A taxpayer encounters a neutral laptop service error and records time, error details and next action with adviser.

sources.label: GOV.UK — Use Making Tax Digital for Income Tax - Help and support - Guidance
GOV.UK — Disagree with a tax decision or penalty: Reasonable excuses
GOV.UK — Issue 148 of agent update

content:
Identify whether the failure is in your software, authorisation, internet connection or HMRC’s service. Save dated evidence and use the appropriate support route. Complete the obligation as soon as possible; an error message alone does not guarantee a penalty appeal will succeed.

Identify where the problem sits

Check your connection and sign-in details, then the software provider's service information. Check HMRC's published service status through GOV.UK as well. HMRC's October 2026 agent update points users to its consolidated live service issues information.

If your accountant is filing, send the error wording and time of the problem. Avoid sharing passwords or security codes. The accountant should check the filing software and the relevant HMRC authorisation before repeatedly attempting the same submission.

Keep a useful incident record

Record when you first tried, the affected business and period, the error shown, relevant service notices and any support reference. Save screenshots that identify the issue without exposing unnecessary personal data.

For example, evidence that a particular service was unavailable when an otherwise complete submission was attempted is more helpful than a message saying only that the website was slow. Keep a note of when the service became available and what happened next.

Complete the outstanding obligation promptly

An outage does not mean the update has been received. Confirm the actual outcome after service resumes and keep the successful submission evidence. Do not send a duplicate purely because your progress screen is delayed.

Check the rules for the relevant year

HMRC does not apply late-quarterly-update penalty points for 2026/27, but the updates remain required. That treatment does not remove annual return or tax payment obligations. For other penalties, a reasonable-excuse claim depends on the facts and HMRC's rules; an outage is not an automatic guarantee of cancellation.

Contact your accountant early when an issue remains unresolved. TaxSimba can explain what information is needed for work within your engagement and help distinguish an outstanding filing from a display or access problem. Waiting until the last available minute leaves less time to investigate either.

Keep a useful failure record

Illustrative preparation example.

Record the attempted filing time, affected business, obligation, error message and support reference. Check whether authorisation, local connectivity or HMRC service status explains it. Keep the eventual successful submission separately; a support ticket alone does not prove the filing finished.

Check: Who owns the fault investigation and when will submission success be verified?

Actions to take
CheckPractical action
Connection, access or service outage?Check the relevant provider and HMRC status rather than guessing from a generic error.
What evidence shows the attempted submission?Record time, period, exact error and support references without unnecessary sensitive data.
What happened after recovery?Confirm the actual receipt status and complete any outstanding obligation promptly.

Should I repeatedly resend until the dashboard changes?

First check the submission outcome. A delayed display is different from a failed filing and repeated attempts can confuse the trail.

Does an outage automatically cancel every penalty?

No. Relevant concessions and reasonable-excuse rules depend on the year and facts. Keep evidence and follow the notice's appeal process if needed.

title: Dividend Tax: Keep Your 2025/26 Return Separate From 2026/27 Rates
excerpt: Dividend tax rates changed from 6 April 2026. If you are preparing a 2025/26 return now, do not use the newer rates simply because they appear in a current tax calculator.
metaTitle: Dividend Tax: Keep 2025/26 and 2026/27 Separate | TaxSimba
metaDescription: Dividend tax rates differ between 2025/26 and 2026/27. Organise vouchers and investment statements by tax year before checking bands and allowances.
featuredImageAlt: A company shareholder separates dividend vouchers into two tax-year folders while checking different-year documents.

sources.label: GOV.UK — Tax on dividends: Check if you have to pay tax on dividends
GOV.UK — Income Tax rates and allowances for current and previous tax years
GOV.UK — Tax on dividends: Check if you have to pay tax on dividends

content:
Use the dividend rates for the year the dividends belong to. The ordinary and upper rates differ between 2025/26 and 2026/27, while the £500 allowance applies in both. Provide vouchers and investment statements so the return uses the right year and income bands.

Which rates belong to which year?

For 2025/26, the dividend ordinary, upper and additional rates are 8.75%, 33.75% and 39.35%. For 2026/27, they are 10.75%, 35.75% and 39.35%. The dividend allowance is £500 in both years. The rate applying to a particular dividend depends on your wider income and available tax bands.

Dividends received between 6 April 2025 and 5 April 2026 belong to the return normally due online by 31 January 2027. Dividends in the following tax year need their own calculation. Do not combine the two years because the same company paid them.

The allowance does not remove the reporting question

Dividends within an ISA are treated differently from dividends outside it. An allowance covering some dividend income also does not mean every taxpayer can ignore dividend information when preparing a return.

If you already complete Self Assessment, give the accountant the full dividend figures. The information is needed to establish the complete income position and apply the allowance correctly.

Gather more than bank transfers

For your own company, provide dividend vouchers and the relevant company records. For investments, obtain tax-year dividend statements from each provider. A transfer labelled drawings is not automatically a lawful dividend, and money paid into your account may need a different explanation.

A useful check before approval

Compare the return's dividend total with your vouchers and investment statements, then check that the calculation uses the year being filed. Where dividends span tax bands, a single headline percentage will not explain the whole result.

TaxSimba can prepare your personal tax return within the agreed scope. Company accounts, dividend legality and director's loan issues may require separate work, so raise those matters before assuming that a personal return package covers them.

Allocate each dividend to its actual tax year

Illustrative preparation example.

A company statement spans March and April. List payment dates and vouchers instead of applying one year’s rates to the whole statement. Keep dividends from other holdings visible too, because the tax calculation concerns the person’s combined income.

Check: Which dividend belongs in 2025/26 and which belongs in 2026/27?

Actions to take
CheckPractical action
Which tax year contains each dividend?Use the actual relevant dates and supporting vouchers or statements.
Which year's rates and allowance apply?Check the calculation for the year being filed rather than today's default calculator.
Does other income use part of the tax bands?Review the full personal income picture before applying a single percentage.

Does the dividend allowance make the income irrelevant to a return?

No. Supply the full relevant dividend information so the annual calculation and reporting can be completed correctly.

Are all company withdrawals dividends?

No. The underlying records and lawful treatment matter. Obtain clarification of salary, loans or other transfers.

title: Student and Postgraduate Loans on Self Assessment: Avoid Double Counting
excerpt: Self Assessment can include student and postgraduate loan repayments as well as Income Tax. If repayments have already been deducted from your salary, the return must take those deductions into account correctly.
metaTitle: Student Loans on Self Assessment: Avoid Double Counting | TaxSimba
metaDescription: Prepare the right student and postgraduate loan plan details, payroll deductions and repayment-start information for a complete Self Assessment calculation.
featuredImageAlt: A graduate compares payroll loan deductions with loan-plan correspondence and yearly return records.

sources.label: GOV.UK — Tell HMRC about a student or postgraduate loan in your tax return
GOV.UK — Repaying your student loan: How to repay

content:
Give the accountant your student-loan plan, any postgraduate loan and repayments already deducted through payroll. Self Assessment can include a further repayment calculation. A loan deduction on a payslip must not be ignored or confused with Income Tax already paid.

Confirm your loan plan first

Check your Student Loans Company information and the repayment plan that applies to the tax year. Do not choose a plan just because a friend started university at a similar time. Postgraduate loans can apply alongside an undergraduate loan, and the return needs the correct information about both.

Use the rates and thresholds for the year being filed. Different plans have different thresholds, so an estimate made using the wrong plan can give a misleading result. HMRC's return guidance also checks whether repayments were due to start on or before 6 April of that tax year; a newly issued loan does not automatically mean repayments are already due.

Include deductions already made through payroll

Give your accountant your P60 and relevant payslips showing student and postgraduate loan deductions. These amounts are not the same as PAYE Income Tax. Entering payroll deductions in the wrong place can lead to an incorrect remaining liability.

For example, someone employed during the week and self-employed at weekends may already have paid through payroll. The annual calculation can still produce an additional repayment because it takes account of relevant income reported on the return.

Explain direct payments and balance changes

Tell the accountant if you made voluntary payments directly to the Student Loans Company, paid off a balance or received instructions to stop deductions. Do not automatically treat a voluntary payment as an offset against a Self Assessment repayment; the correct treatment needs checking.

If your loan is nearly repaid, compare the return position with the latest loan information and ask how any potential overpayment will be resolved. HMRC and the Student Loans Company have different roles in that process.

Review the calculation as a whole

A larger-than-expected bill is not always extra Income Tax. Ask for the student loan, postgraduate loan, National Insurance and tax components to be explained separately.

TaxSimba can use the plan details and evidence you provide when preparing your return. Supply them early, particularly where employment deductions or a recent repayment make the year-end position less straightforward.

Reconcile payroll loan deductions separately

Illustrative preparation example.

Collect the P60 or payslip evidence of student and postgraduate loan deductions and identify the relevant plans. Keep those figures separate from PAYE Income Tax. Otherwise the return can miss a repayment already made or mislabel it as ordinary tax.

Check: Are all payroll repayments and applicable loan types included in the review?

Actions to take
CheckPractical action
Which plan and repayment start apply?Use Student Loans Company evidence for the tax year.
What did payroll already deduct?Provide student and postgraduate amounts separately from PAYE Income Tax.
Were there direct payments or a cleared balance?Flag them for review instead of treating them as automatic offsets.

Can postgraduate and undergraduate repayments both apply?

Yes, depending on the loans and circumstances. Supply details of both rather than selecting only one.

Is a larger bill necessarily extra Income Tax?

No. Ask for tax, National Insurance, student loan and postgraduate loan components to be shown separately.

title: Self-Employed National Insurance for Your 2025/26 Tax Return
excerpt: Your Self Assessment bill may include National Insurance as well as Income Tax. For a 2025/26 sole trader return, use that year's thresholds rather than copying the figures currently displayed for 2026/27.
metaTitle: Self-Employed National Insurance 2025/26: Check the Year | TaxSimba
metaDescription: Check Class 4 and Class 2 treatment for your 2025/26 tax return using the correct year's profit figures, employment records and contribution history.
featuredImageAlt: A self-employed worker checks profit records and National Insurance correspondence with accountant, no rate numbers.

sources.label: GOV.UK — Rates and allowances: National Insurance contributions
GOV.UK — National Insurance: introduction: National Insurance classes
GOV.UK — Self-employed National Insurance rates

content:
For a 2025/26 sole trader return, Class 4 generally applies at 6% between £12,570 and £50,270 of profits and 2% above that. Class 2 can be treated as paid without a charge when the year’s conditions are met. Check the historic rates and your contribution position.

Class 4 is based on taxable trading profits

For 2025/26, Class 4 is generally 6% on profits over £12,570 up to £50,270, and 2% above £50,270. Other rules can affect the calculation, including age and interaction with employment contributions.

Turnover and profit are different. A trader with £40,000 of sales does not normally calculate Class 4 on the full £40,000 if allowable business costs reduce the taxable profit.

Class 2 does not always mean a separate charge

For 2025/26, qualifying self-employed profits of £6,845 or more generally mean Class 2 is treated as paid to protect the National Insurance record, without a Class 2 payment. Below that level, voluntary Class 2 may be available at £3.50 a week, subject to the relevant conditions.

Do not assume that a voluntary payment is beneficial merely because the option appears. Check your contribution record, existing credits and eligibility before deciding whether to pay. Equally, do not assume that low profit automatically gives you a qualifying year.

Tell the accountant about employment too

If you were employed and self-employed in the same year, provide your P60 and trading records. Employment contributions and self-employed contributions interact under rules that a simple single-income estimate may not capture.

Ordinary residential rental income is not automatically subject to the same National Insurance treatment as a sole trade. Explain what you actually do rather than describing every income source as self-employment.

Check the components before paying

Ask how much of the bill is Income Tax, Class 4 and any voluntary Class 2. Payments on account can also make the amount due differ from the year's liability.

TaxSimba can prepare the return using the relevant year and your full income information. Keep National Insurance questions separate from the monthly fee paid for an MTD accounting service; one is a government liability and the other pays for professional work.

Use profit and the correct contribution year

Illustrative preparation example.

Keep the tax-adjusted trade profit calculation and any information relevant to contribution status. Bank drawings, turnover and profit are different amounts. Before using a National Insurance rate, check that it belongs to the return year being prepared.

Check: Which profit figure and tax-year rules support the contribution calculation?

Actions to take
CheckPractical action
Are the profit figures tax-adjusted?Separate gross sales, allowable costs and any further adjustments.
Is the calculation using 2025/26 rules?Do not copy current-year Class 2 figures into an earlier return.
Does other employment or age affect the position?Supply the full contribution context and check the NI record where relevant.

Is every Class 2 entry an extra weekly bill?

No. Depending on the year's profit and conditions, Class 2 may be treated as paid. Check the relevant year and eligibility.

Should I always pay voluntary contributions for a low-profit year?

Check the contribution record, existing credits and eligibility first. A voluntary payment is not automatically useful in every case.

title: Cash Basis or Traditional Accounting: Which Figures Go on Your Return?
excerpt: Your accounting method affects when income and expenses appear in your tax calculation. Cash basis and traditional accounting can produce different figures even when they relate to the same business activity.
metaTitle: Cash Basis vs Traditional Accounting: Timing Matters | TaxSimba
metaDescription: Compare cash basis with traditional accounting, identify unpaid invoices and bills, and check opening adjustments before switching methods.
featuredImageAlt: A consultant compares an unpaid invoice with a later bank receipt on a two-period timeline.

sources.label: GOV.UK — Business records if you're self-employed: Overview
GOV.UK — Cash basis: Overview
GOV.UK — HS222 How to calculate your taxable profits (2026)

content:
Cash basis generally follows money received and paid; traditional accounting follows income earned and expenses incurred. The method affects timing, not whether the bank balance is correct. Check eligibility and transition adjustments before changing methods or copying last year’s workings.

Cash basis follows money received and paid

Under cash basis, income is generally recorded when received and expenses when paid, subject to the tax rules. It became the default accounting method for eligible sole traders and partnerships from 2024/25. Businesses can choose traditional accounting where appropriate, and some are not eligible for cash basis.

An unpaid invoice at 5 April can therefore be treated differently from one that has already been paid. The date you completed the work alone does not establish the cash-basis receipt date.

Traditional accounting follows a different timing approach

Traditional accounting generally recognises income earned and costs incurred for the accounting period, including relevant amounts still unpaid. It can involve debtors, creditors, stock and adjustments that do not appear directly in bank transactions.

For example, an invoice issued in March and paid in May should not simply be moved between years without checking the method. Both methods require a consistent, supportable calculation.

Switching needs a proper reconciliation

Changing method can require adjustments so income and costs are neither omitted nor counted twice. Provide the previous accounts and tax computation before a new accountant prepares the next return. Do not switch merely by selecting a different software option.

Equipment, finance costs, losses and unusual receipts can also require specific treatment. An accounting method is not a general permission to deduct everything leaving the bank.

MTD does not choose the tax treatment for you

Keeping records digitally and sending quarterly summaries are separate from deciding the correct annual taxable profit. The accountant still needs to know the method used and any year-end adjustments required.

Tell TaxSimba which method was used previously and supply outstanding invoices, bills and relevant opening balances. Where you are unsure, provide the last accounts rather than guessing. Establishing the method first makes the return easier to review and reduces the risk of the same transaction appearing in two tax years.

Follow one invoice across the year end

Illustrative preparation example.

An invoice is issued before 5 April but paid afterwards. Keep the invoice and receipt dates visible so the accounting method determines the reporting year. When changing methods, check the transition so the same amount is neither omitted nor counted twice.

Check: Which method applies, and was the amount already brought into an earlier calculation?

Actions to take
CheckPractical action
Which method was used previously?Locate the prior accounts and return rather than guessing from the software screen.
What remains unpaid at year-end?List invoices, bills and relevant stock or balances.
Is a method change proposed?Prepare the transition reconciliation and confirm eligibility and adjustments first.

Does using a bank feed mean I use cash basis?

No. A record source does not itself establish the accounting method. Confirm the method applied in the tax calculation.

Can I switch just by moving an invoice into next year's folder?

No. Timing and transition rules need consistent treatment supported by the records.

title: Made a Self-Employed Loss? What to Check Before Claiming Relief
excerpt: A business loss does not automatically produce a tax refund. First establish the tax-adjusted loss, then check which reliefs are available and whether a claim would actually benefit you.
metaTitle: Self-Employed Trading Loss: Compare Relief Options | TaxSimba
metaDescription: A trading loss does not guarantee a refund. Establish the tax-adjusted loss, gather earlier returns and compare eligible relief routes and deadlines.
featuredImageAlt: A sole trader brings loss-making business accounts to an adviser to review available options rather than guaranteed refund.

sources.label: GOV.UK — HS227 Losses (2026)

content:
A trading loss is not automatically a refund. Work out the tax-adjusted loss, then compare the reliefs available, their deadlines and the other income involved. Keep the supporting accounts and earlier claims so the same loss is not used twice.

A cash shortfall is not always a tax loss

Loan repayments, drawings and private spending can reduce the bank balance without being deductible business expenses. Equipment and other costs may need particular treatment. Your accountant should calculate the taxable result before choosing any loss-relief route.

For example, a trader may spend heavily on personal living costs while taking little money from customers. That financial pressure does not establish an allowable trading loss of the same amount.

Different reliefs serve different situations

Depending on the circumstances, a qualifying loss may be carried forward against future profits of the same trade or considered against other income. Special rules can apply to early trading losses, terminal losses and claims involving earlier years.

Conditions, claim deadlines and restrictions vary. Commerciality, the nature of the trade and particular loss-relief limits matter. Foreign trades and claims under the foreign income and gains regime can add further restrictions.

Compare the effect before making a claim

A claim against another year's income might reduce tax, but the result depends on that year's income, allowances and existing reliefs. Using a loss immediately is not necessarily the most useful option. An accountant should compare the available choices rather than assume the largest loss gives the largest refund.

Loss relief is also different from reducing payments on account. The two may interact, but changing future payments does not itself make or establish a loss claim.

Documents your accountant needs

Supply accounts, detailed income and expenses, the trading start date, previous returns, other income and any losses already carried forward. If the business has stopped, give the cessation date and explain outstanding receipts or costs.

TaxSimba can confirm whether the relevant loss calculation and claims are within the agreed service. Ask about additional work involving earlier years before proceeding. A supported claim is more valuable than an advert promising a refund before anyone has examined the records.

Name the relief route before calculating a repayment

  • Current or previous-year income: eligible losses can be considered against the relevant income, subject to restrictions.
  • Future profits of the same trade: unused qualifying losses may be carried forward.
  • Early trade losses: the first four trading years can involve special carry-back rules.
  • Terminal losses: a qualifying loss in the final 12 months can be set against relevant trade profits, with a specific carry-back order.

Use HMRC’s 2025/26 loss helpsheet for the applicable claims, deadlines and restrictions. General-income claims can affect allowances; partial claims are not freely selectable. Record the claim and unused balance. Overseas trades with a FIG claim need separate checking.

Compare relief routes using the actual tax years

Illustrative preparation example.

Keep the supported loss beside other income and tax paid for the relevant years. Compare the available claims and their effect on allowances before choosing one. Record the amount used and balance remaining so later returns do not claim the same loss again.

Check: Which route is eligible, what is its deadline and what loss remains afterwards?

Actions to take
CheckPractical action
Is there a supported tax loss?Remove non-deductible private and capital items and check the accounting treatment.
Which relief routes are available?Review conditions, deadlines and prior claims for the trade.
What is the effect across relevant years?Compare available relief rather than assuming the fastest refund is the best outcome.

Does every loss create a repayment?

No. A repayment depends on the available relief, income and tax paid. Some relief may be carried forward instead.

Does reducing payments on account make a loss claim?

No. Advance-payment estimates and formal loss-relief claims are separate processes.

title: Stopped Being Self-Employed? Your Final Return Still Matters
excerpt: Stopping work as a sole trader does not automatically close your Self Assessment obligations. You need to tell HMRC, complete the relevant final return and deal with records or amounts remaining after the business stops.
metaTitle: Stopped Self-Employed? Prepare Your Final Tax Return | TaxSimba
metaDescription: Closing a sole trade still needs HMRC notification and final tax work. Gather cessation dates, unpaid amounts, assets and any remaining MTD obligations.
featuredImageAlt: A closing business owner packs equipment and checks final accounts, cessation date and outstanding return with adviser.

sources.label: GOV.UK — Stop being self-employed
GOV.UK — Use Making Tax Digital for Income Tax - Add or cease income sources - Guidance

content:
Tell HMRC when you stop self-employment and complete the relevant final return. Outstanding receipts, costs, assets and MTD updates can still need attention. Stopping one trade also does not end Self Assessment if another income source requires it.

Establish the actual cessation date

The date you stopped trading may differ from the date the last customer paid. Give your accountant a timeline covering the final work, invoices, receipts and remaining business assets. The accounting method affects how outstanding amounts are treated.

Use HMRC's process to report that you have stopped being self-employed. Closing a business bank account or cancelling a website does not notify HMRC on your behalf.

Prepare the final taxable result

Include the relevant income and allowable expenses, and review stock, equipment, unpaid amounts and any loss relief. A transfer of the business into a limited company needs particular attention; it is not always a simple closure with no tax consequences.

For example, a trader stopping in February 2026 may still need a 2025/26 return due online by 31 January 2027. Waiting until the next year to tell an accountant can make missing records harder to recover.

MTD businesses have additional closing steps

If the business is within MTD, HMRC's guidance requires the cessation to be recorded and the final relevant quarterly update to be sent. The income still belongs in the annual return for the year it ceased. Other continuing trades or rental businesses may remain within MTD.

Do not simply stop submitting because there were no new customers. A permanent cessation and a quiet trading period are different situations.

Check whether Self Assessment continues

You might still need returns for rent, gains or other income after self-employment ends. Conversely, if no return is needed, ask HMRC to confirm the change rather than ignoring an issued filing notice.

Tell TaxSimba the closure date, what has already been reported and whether other income continues. The accountant can confirm the final-year work, any earlier outstanding returns and the information needed to close the reporting position properly.

Keep a closure list beyond the last sale

Illustrative preparation example.

Record the cessation date, unpaid invoices, remaining stock or equipment and outstanding returns. Check any MTD duties and transition balances separately. Stopping customer work does not automatically close every tax task or remove another source of reportable income.

Check: Which final receipts, asset matters and reporting obligations remain open?

CheckPractical action
When did the trade actually cease?Prepare a timeline of final work, invoices and receipts.
What remains to be accounted for?Identify unpaid amounts, assets, stock and any final-year loss questions.
Do other reporting duties continue?Check other income, final MTD updates and existing notices to file.

Does cancelling my business website close Self Assessment?

No. Follow HMRC's notification process and complete required final filings.

Can one ceased trade end MTD for my continuing rental business?

Not automatically. Each continuing source and the overall reporting position need checking.

title: Content Creator Tax: Sponsorships, Platform Income and Gifted Products
excerpt: Content creation can produce taxable income even when a brand pays with products or services instead of cash. Keep records of the commercial arrangement, not just payments arriving in your bank account.
metaTitle: Content Creator Tax: Cash, Sponsorships and Products | TaxSimba
metaDescription: Prepare creator tax records for advertising, affiliates, sponsorships and non-cash collaborations, with platform reconciliations and private-use details.
featuredImageAlt: A content creator organises sponsorship agreements, platform earnings and gifted-product records beside a camera.

sources.label: GOV.UK — Check if you need to tell HMRC about your income from online platforms

content:
Record platform earnings, sponsorships, affiliate fees and commercial payments made in products or services. A gifted item can need a different assessment from an unsolicited personal gift. Keep the agreement and valuation evidence rather than looking only at bank deposits.

Identify the different income streams

Advertising revenue, paid partnerships, affiliate commissions, subscriptions and direct customer payments may all need considering. A product supplied in exchange for promotional work can also have a value for tax purposes.

HMRC's online-platform guidance explains that where gifts or services are received instead of money, their value is relevant. Distinguish a commercial exchange from a genuinely unrelated personal gift; the description used by a brand does not settle the treatment.

Keep evidence behind each collaboration

Save contracts, emails, campaign briefs, invoices, payout statements and details of non-cash items. Note what you agreed to provide, when you received the consideration and how a reasonable value was established.

For example, a hotel stay provided in exchange for promotional posts is not automatically invisible to tax because no cash changed hands. The facts of the arrangement and any genuinely allowable costs need separate review.

Platform payouts can hide deductions

A platform may retain fees before transferring money. Keep the full statement so gross receipts and relevant costs can be reconciled. Avoid counting the bank payout and the underlying platform sale as two separate items of income.

Business and personal use also need distinguishing for phones, equipment, travel and subscriptions. Creating content during a personal holiday does not automatically turn every holiday cost into a business deduction.

Check the reporting route

The trading allowance, Self Assessment registration and MTD eligibility have different tests. If a platform reports information to HMRC, that does not automatically calculate or pay your tax for you.

Tell TaxSimba about all platforms, brand arrangements and other income, including employment. The accountant can confirm the appropriate service and what records are needed. Where foreign payments or complex arrangements are involved, establish the scope before purchase rather than assuming a simple-return package covers every issue.

Keep the agreement behind a non-cash payment

Illustrative preparation example.

A brand provides a product in exchange for a post. Keep the agreement, product details and valuation evidence with cash sponsorship and affiliate records. The absence of a bank receipt does not establish that the arrangement has no tax relevance.

Check: What was provided, what work was agreed and what evidence supports the value?

CheckPractical action

Can platform income be reconciled?Keep gross receipts, fees, refunds and payouts without duplication.
Are costs partly personal?Provide purpose and mixed-use facts before claiming travel, clothing or equipment.

Do non-cash collaborations always escape tax?

No. A commercial exchange can have taxable value without a bank payment. Explain the full arrangement.

Does platform reporting calculate my tax?

No. You still need complete records and the correct reporting position across all platforms and income streams.

excerpt: Tutoring income can come from direct lessons, agencies and online platforms. Before preparing a return, establish whether each arrangement is employment or self-employment and keep the evidence supporting that treatment.

content:
Keep private lesson income separate from any employed teaching role. Record gross fees, cancellations, refunds and platform charges, including cash lessons. Explain the working arrangements before assuming every tutoring payment is self-employed income.

Separate school employment from private work

A tutor may be paid through PAYE by a school and receive separate private lesson fees. The employment income belongs with the employment records; genuine self-employed activity needs its own business calculation.

An agency calling you self-employed does not, by itself, settle employment status. Keep the contract and explain who sets the work, controls the arrangement and pays you if the position is uncertain.

Record the full lesson income

Keep a schedule of fees, cancellations, refunds and amounts received through platforms. Platform charges may be deducted before payout, so retain statements showing the underlying lesson income and fees.

If a parent pays for a block of lessons, note what the payment covers and any refund conditions. The accounting method affects timing; do not move receipts between tax years simply to match school terms.

Review business costs carefully

Relevant teaching materials, platform charges, insurance and a reasonable business portion of certain running costs may be deductible where the rules are met. Private costs and mixed-use equipment need review rather than a blanket percentage copied from another tutor.

Travel also needs checking. A journey related to tutoring is not automatically deductible under every working arrangement, and the rules differ from an employee expense claim.

Prepare for the correct tax year

For a 2025/26 online return, gather records covering 6 April 2025 to 5 April 2026; the usual filing deadline is 31 January 2027. Summer holidays and the academic year do not change those tax-year boundaries.

Tell TaxSimba about employment, private pupils, agency contracts and platform income. The accountant can then confirm the scope and review the information needed for your return. If gross self-employment income grows, check MTD separately instead of waiting until the next annual filing season to consider it.

Reconcile tutoring platforms with private lessons

Illustrative preparation example.

Keep platform statements, direct lesson fees, cancellations and refunds together, but distinguish any employed teaching role. Gross fees and net platform payouts answer different questions. A full appointment record helps identify cash lessons missing from bank deposits.

metaDescription: Prepare personal trainer tax records for gym work, client packages and online coaching, with clear refunds, fees, employment and business-cost evidence.
featuredImageAlt: A personal trainer reconciles prepaid client sessions, gym rent and online coaching statements, modest weights nearby.

sources.label: GOV.UK — Working for yourself
